docs.title: fastEIT
docs.text:
Python library for electrical impedance tomography (EIT) recordings of the Dräger PulmoVista 500 and of Timpel: it reads the files, prepares each breath and computes the clinical indices of tidal recordings and PEEP trials, as tables ready for statistical analysis.

Research use only

fastEIT is for research. It is not a medical device and has not been validated for clinical decisions.

docs.title: From a file to the clinical indices
docs.text:
Each layer returns one object that holds the object of the layer before it:

Dräger .bin, Timpel .csv / .txt / .asc
 └─ load_data() ───────────► ReconstructedFrameData   layer 1: the file as it is (32x32 images)
     └─ preprocess() ──────► EITRecording             layer 2: the measured breaths
          ├─ tidal_features() ───────► TidalFeatures       layer 3: indices
          └─ segment_peep_trial() ───► PeepTrial           layer 2b: PEEP steps
               └─ peep_trial_features() ► PeepTrialFeatures  layer 3: indices
                    └─ recording_tables() ► tables, CSV        layer 4: export

The pipeline starts from reconstructed images. A Dräger .eit file holds the raw measurements (RawImpedanceData, 208 transimpedances per frame) and needs a reconstruction first; a Dräger .asc export holds signals only (ContinuousSignalData) and has no images (parsers).

Layer What it does How it works 1. Parsers Dräger .bin, .eit, .asc and Timpel files to data containers Parsers 2. Preprocessing cardiac filter, breaths with quality flags, exclusions, lung mask, regions; auxiliary signals in cmH2O, L/s, mL; PEEP, plateau, driving pressure and tidal volume of each breath Preprocessing 2b. Segmentation PEEP steps from the pressure or placed by hand, breaths analysed, driving pressure and tidal volume of each step Segmentation 3. Clinical indices EELI, TIV, share by region, GI, centre of ventilation, compliance, Costa collapse and overdistension, changes between steps, recruitment-to-inflation ratio Clinical indices 4. Export one row per recording, breath and PEEP step, keyed by patient, recording and phase; a whole study at once; CSV ready for statistical analysis Export

Every method states its source (paper and DOI, or the evidence notebook) and the reimplemented steps are checked against eitprocessing.

Start with the user guide: install and supported files, then analyse a recording, cut a recording, check it with the review figures and export the tables. The pages under "How it works" describe each layer and its choices; every function is in the API reference.

docs.title: Contributing to fastEIT
docs.text: Every contribution is welcome - whether it is a bug report, a new parser, a documentation fix, or just a question. This is an open project and there is no wrong way to get involved, as long as you bring curiosity and a collaborative attitude. If you are unsure whether your idea fits, open an issue and let's talk about it.

docs.title: Reporting bugs
docs.text: Open a GitHub issue with: - Python version and OS - Minimal code that reproduces the problem - Full traceback

docs.title: Requesting features
docs.text: Open a GitHub issue describing the use case and the expected behaviour.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Kernel236/fastEIT.git
cd fastEIT
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
This project uses ruff for linting and formatting.

ruff check src/ tests/
ruff format src/ tests/

GitHub Actions runs ruff check and ruff format --check on every pull request to dev or main, and on every push to those branches.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs from docs/ and from the docstrings of the code (Google style). To see it while editing:

pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve

A pull request is checked with mkdocs build --strict: a broken link or a docstring parameter that is not in the signature fails the build.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
pytest tests/

Tests that require real patient files are skipped automatically if the files are not present (they are gitignored). Use pytest -rs to see which tests were skipped and why.

docs.title: Adding a new parser
docs.text: See docs/parsing_layer.md for a step-by-step recipe covering detection, schema definition, parser class, loader registration, and the testing checklist.

docs.title: Pull request process
docs.text:
Please open a GitHub issue to discuss your idea before opening a PR.

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch from dev
  2. Make your changes with tests
  3. Ensure ruff check, ruff format --check and pytest pass locally
  4. Open a PR targeting dev (not main)
  5. Describe what changed and why

docs.text: This project follows the Contributor Covenant.

docs.title: fastEIT - Data Model
docs.text:
Specifications for all data containers. For parser details, calibration constants, and loader utilities see parsers.md. For architecture and extension recipes see parsing_layer.md.

All containers of layer 1 inherit from BaseData (models/base_data.py). The objects of the later layers are in section 5.

docs.title: 1. BaseData - common base
docs.text:
filename    str          Source file path
file_format str          "bin" | "eit" | "asc" | "csv" | "txt"
vendor      str          "draeger" | "timpel"
fs          float|None   Sampling frequency in Hz (parser-derived)
metadata    dict         Header fields, firmware version, warnings, etc.
n_frames    int          Set by subclass __post_init__ - never passed by caller
duration    float        n_frames / fs  (0.0 if fs is None)

docs.title: 2. ReconstructedFrameData
docs.text:
File: models/reconstructed_data.py Produced by: DragerBinParser (.bin), TimpelTabularParser (.csv/.txt/.asc)

frames      np.ndarray   Structured array shape (N,). Named fields:
                           ts            float64   timestamp (unit depends on vendor, see below)
                           pixels        float32   32×32 image per frame
                         Dräger .bin only:
                           min_max_flag  int32     +1=insp peak, -1=exp trough, 0=none
                           event_marker  int32     event counter
                           event_text    S30       ASCII event string, space- or null-padded
                           timing_error  int32     0 = ok

aux_signals dict|None    Named arrays, each shape (N,), frame-aligned with frames.
                         Dräger .bin: 52 or 58 Medibus channels, sentinel values
                         left unchanged (replaced in preprocessing).
                         Units of the device (parser tables MEDIBUS_UNITS,
                         TIMPEL_AUX_UNITS); preprocessing converts them to the
                         same units for every vendor (cmH2O, L/s, mL).
                         Timpel: 6 device channels (airway_pressure, flow,
                         volume, min_flag, max_flag, qrs_flag - cols 1024-1029).
                         None if the source file carries no auxiliary signals.

Property accessors:

data.timestamps      # frames["ts"]           shape (N,)
data.pixels          # frames["pixels"]        shape (N, 32, 32)
data.min_max_flags   # frames["min_max_flag"]  shape (N,)  - Dräger .bin only
data.event_markers   # frames["event_marker"]  shape (N,)  - Dräger .bin only
data.event_texts     # frames["event_text"]    shape (N,)  - Dräger .bin only
data.global_signal   # pixels.sum(axis=(1,2))  shape (N,)
data.roi_signals     # 4 horizontal strips     shape (N, 4)
data.roi_signal(n)   # single ROI 0-3          shape (N,)

global_signal and roi_signals are raw sums with no lung mask - the mask is applied in the preprocessing layer. They sum the values as stored, Dräger "no data" values included. On the parsed file, fasteit.preprocessing.pipeline has:

  • global_impedance(raw) - the sum of the pixels with a value, NaN where a frame has missing pixels (the frames preprocess() excludes), read in blocks for long files;
  • pixel_values(raw, index) - the pixels of some frames, "no data" values as NaN;
  • recording_time(raw) - the time of each frame from the device clock. duration is n_frames / fs: when the device dropped frames, the file lasts a little longer.

Timestamp conventions:

Vendor ts field Unit Dräger .bin wall-clock time from device, stored as-is fraction of day (× 86400 for seconds) Timpel .csv synthetic: (frame_index + first_frame) / 50.0 seconds from start

docs.title: 3. ContinuousSignalData
docs.text:
File: models/continuous_data.py Produced by: DragerAscParser (.asc)

table   pd.DataFrame   One row per EIT frame. Snake_case column names.
                       Dräger .asc columns include:
                         image, time, global, local_1_x_16_y_29 ... local_4_x_16_y_05
                         minmax, event, eventtext, timing_error
                         + Medibus channels when ventilator is connected via Medibus

n_frames = len(table). duration = n_frames / fs.

docs.title: 4. RawImpedanceData
docs.text:
File: models/raw_impedance_data.py Produced by: DragerEitParser (.eit)

measurements   np.ndarray   shape (N_frames, 208)
                            Calibrated transimpedances (not raw ADC counts, not
                            yet image-reconstructed). For Dräger:
                            vv = FT_A*trans_A - FT_B*trans_B (EIDORS, Adler 2016)
                            208 = 16 electrodes × 13 measurement pairs
                            (adjacent drive, standard Dräger pattern)

aux_signals    dict|None    Named per-frame arrays. Populated by DragerEitParser:
                              "timestamp"          float64 (N,)    fraction of day
                              "trans_A"            float64 (N,208) raw ADC - primary
                              "trans_B"            float64 (N,208) raw ADC - reference
                              "injection_current"  float64 (N,16)  raw ADC counts
                              "I_real"             float64 (N,16)  injected current [A]
                              "voltage_A"          float64 (N,16)  raw ADC counts
                              "voltage_B"          float64 (N,16)  raw ADC counts
                              "V_diff"             float64 (N,16)  differential voltage [V]
                              "frame_counter"      uint16  (N,)
                              "medibus"            float32 (N,67)  ventilator channels
                            None if the source file carries no auxiliary signals.

Intended consumer: reconstruct_greit() (in fasteit.parsers.draeger.eit.eit_pyeit_bridge, requires optional pyeit dependency) or any external reconstruction library. For .bin and Timpel .csv files, fastEIT ingests vendor-reconstructed images and does not re-reconstruct them.

docs.title: 5. From a file to the clinical indices
docs.text:
Each layer returns one object that holds the object of the layer before it, so the last one holds everything:

Dräger .bin, Timpel .csv / .txt / .asc
 └─ load_data() ───────────► ReconstructedFrameData   layer 1: the file as it is (32x32 images)
     └─ preprocess() ──────► EITRecording             layer 2: the measured breaths
          ├─ tidal_features() ───────► TidalFeatures       layer 3: indices
          └─ segment_peep_trial() ───► PeepTrial           layer 2b: PEEP steps
               └─ peep_trial_features() ► PeepTrialFeatures  layer 3: indices
                    └─ recording_tables() ► tables, CSV        layer 4: export

The pipeline starts from reconstructed images. A Dräger .eit file holds the raw measurements (RawImpedanceData, 208 transimpedances per frame) and needs a reconstruction first; a Dräger .asc export holds signals only (ContinuousSignalData) and has no images (parsers).

Each value is stored once, in the table of the layer that produces it; tables are joined on breath_id, step (with peep) and region.

Where One row per Content EITRecording.breaths breath times and frames, quality flags, excluded, is_valid, PEEP, plateau, driving pressure, measured tidal volume EITRecording.aux (+ aux_units) frame auxiliary signals in cmH2O, L/s, mL; device markers EITRecording arrays - pixels, lung_mask, roi_masks, roi_signals, global_signal, time EITRecording.context - RecordingContext: patient_id, label, position, protocol, interface, tidal_volume_ml, notes PeepTrial.breaths breath the breaths of the recording plus peep_step, analysed PeepTrial fields - source ("pressure" or "manual"), phase (the PEEP trial part of the recording, or None), config (SegmentationConfig) PeepTrial.steps step PEEP level measured and of the protocol (peep_set), times, breaths analysed, enough, plateau, driving pressure and tidal volume with their sources TidalFeatures.breaths, PeepTrialFeatures.breaths breath EELI, TIV, GI, centre of ventilation, respiratory rate, tidal volume used, compliance (EIT units and mL/cmH2O) ...Features.regions breath and region EELI, TIV, share, TIV in mL, compliance (EIT units and mL/cmH2O) PeepTrialFeatures.steps step medians of the analysed breaths, compliance and % of the best, collapse, overdistension, changes vs the previous and the first step PeepTrialFeatures.step_regions step and region the regional values of each step TidalFeatures.summary region and index median and quartiles over the valid breaths PeepTrialFeatures.summary region and feature crossing PEEP, best PEEP, R/I steps (global), R/I and recruited volume (global and by region) PeepTrialFeatures.config - AnalysisConfig used (R/I levels)

Layer 4 joins them into flat tables, one row per breath or step with everything, keyed by patient, recording and phase (export.md). Details: preprocessing.md, segmentation.md, features.md.

docs.title: Export for statistical analysis
docs.text:
The export (layer 4) takes the results of an analysis (analyse a recording) and writes them as tables: one analysis at a time, or a whole study at once. In the analysis objects each value is stored once, in the table of the step that computes it; here the tables are joined, so that a breath or a PEEP step is one row with everything. Only recordings that can be analysed (Dräger .bin, Timpel) have tables.

  1. Entry point
  2. Keys: patient, recording, phase
  3. Tables
  4. Column names
  5. CSV files

docs.title: 1. Entry point
docs.text:
from fasteit.export import combine_tables, recording_tables, write_csv
from fasteit.features import peep_trial_features, tidal_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext, Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

context = RecordingContext(patient_id="P01", label="T0", tidal_volume_ml=450)
recording = preprocess(load_data("P01_T0.bin"), context=context)

# A baseline, then a PEEP trial, in the same recording: one analysis per phase.
baseline = tidal_features(recording, phase=Segment(0, 290, "phase", "tidal"))
trial = peep_trial_features(
    segment_peep_trial(recording, phase=Segment(320, 1500, "phase", "peep_trial"))
)

tables = combine_tables([
    recording_tables(baseline, phase="baseline"),
    recording_tables(trial, phase="trial"),
])
write_csv(tables, "results/")   # results/recordings.csv, breaths.csv, steps.csv, ...

The tables on real recordings (11 tidal recordings, four PEEP trials) are in notebooks/08_export.ipynb.

A study is the same call with the analyses of every recording: one or a hundred, the tables are the same. For a simple tidal recording recording_tables(tidal_features(recording)) is enough.

docs.title: 2. Keys: patient, recording, phase
docs.text:
Every row starts with three keys:

Key What Where it comes from patient_id the patient RecordingContext.patient_id label the recording for that patient, e.g. a time point (T0) or a position RecordingContext.label, or recording_tables(..., label="T1") phase the part of the recording analysed recording_tables(..., phase="baseline"); by default the protocol, tidal or peep_trial

By default the phase is the protocol, so a tidal baseline and a PEEP trial of the same recording are told apart already; two parts of the same protocol (e.g. a baseline and a recovery) need a name. Naming every part (baseline, trial) makes the tables easier to read: see cut a recording. combine_tables() refuses two analyses with the same three keys.

The clinical data (side, position, interface, outcome) stay in the case report form and are joined at the time of the analysis on patient_id and label: one row per recording here, one row per patient in R or SPSS (tidyr::pivot_wider() on label).

docs.title: 3. Tables
docs.text:
Table One row per Content recordings analysis protocol, file, vendor, fs, start_time and end_time of the breaths of the phase, n_breaths, n_used, typed tidal_volume_ml, cardiac_filter, fasteit_version; for a PEEP trial its results: crossing PEEP, best PEEP, R/I and recruited volume (global and by half) breaths breath of the phase times, quality flags, excluded, exclusion_label, is_valid, used, PEEP, plateau, driving pressure, measured tidal volume (preprocessing); peep_step, peep_set (PEEP trials); EELI, TIV, GI, centre of ventilation, respiratory rate, tidal volume used, compliance (clinical indices); regional values as columns steps PEEP step (PEEP trials) step, measured peep, peep_set, times, breaths analysed, driving pressure and tidal volume with their sources (segmentation); medians of the breath indices, compliance and % of the best, collapse, overdistension, changes vs the previous and the first step (clinical indices); regional values as columns settings parameter section (fasteit, preprocessing, context, segmentation, analysis), parameter, value: with the file, enough to compute the same values again log message layer (preprocessing, segmentation, indices), level (ok for a check that passed, info, warning), message

Each value once. The tables hold what was measured (one row per breath and per step) and the results of the PEEP-trial methods (Costa collapse and overdistension in steps; crossing PEEP, best PEEP and recruitment-to-inflation ratio, R/I, in recordings, one value per trial). Summaries of these rows are made at analysis time, with the choices of the study (median or mean, which breaths):

breaths |> filter(used == 1) |>
  group_by(patient_id, label, phase) |>
  summarise(across(c(tiv, gi, share__dorsal, compliance_ml), median))   # one row per recording
steps |> pivot_wider(id_cols = c(patient_id, label), names_from = peep_set,
                     values_from = collapse, names_prefix = "collapse_peep")   # one column per level

In SPSS the same are AGGREGATE (breaths to one row per recording) and CASESTOVARS (steps to one column per PEEP level).

Breaths of the phase. Each analysis exports the breaths of its own phase, all of them (also the excluded ones and those between steps), so that in a recording with two phases no breath is exported twice. used marks the breaths that entered the indices: the valid breaths of a tidal phase, the breaths analysed in each step of a PEEP trial.

Steps. The step table is the curve of the trial: with peep_set on the x axis it gives the collapse and overdistension curves (Costa) and the crossing PEEP, and the regional compliance at each PEEP.

library(tidyverse)
steps <- read_csv("results/steps.csv")
ggplot(steps, aes(peep_set)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = collapse)) + geom_line(aes(y = overdistension)) +
  facet_wrap(~ patient_id + label)

docs.title: 4. Column names
docs.text:
Pattern Example Where {index}__{region} tiv__ventral, compliance_ml__left regional values in breaths and steps {feature}__{region} crossing_peep__global, ri__dorsal results of a PEEP trial in recordings

The regions exported are the halves of the lung: ventral, dorsal, right, left (patient right and left); the layers and the quadrants stay in the analysis objects (features.regions) and are not exported. Two underscores separate the index from the region, because an index can contain one (compliance_ml). Back to one row per region in R:

steps |> pivot_longer(contains("__"), names_to = c("index", "region"), names_sep = "__")

Names are in snake case, start with a letter and are shorter than 64 characters, as SPSS requires. Units: pressures in cmH2O, volumes in mL, compliance in EIT units per cmH2O (compliance) and mL/cmH2O (compliance_ml), times in seconds from the start of the file.

docs.title: 5. CSV files
docs.text: write_csv(tables, folder) writes one file per table: UTF-8, comma separated, decimal point, an empty cell for a missing value, booleans as 1 / 0. The files are read without options by R (readr::read_csv()), SPSS (File > Import Data > CSV), Excel and Python. Files with the same name in the folder are replaced. The column file is the name of the source file: rename files whose names hold names or dates before sharing the tables.

docs.title: fastEIT - Clinical Indices (layer 3)
docs.text:
Layer 3 turns a preprocessed recording (EITRecording, preprocessing.md) or a segmented PEEP trial (PeepTrial, segmentation.md) into tables of clinical indices: one row per breath, per breath and region, per PEEP step, per step and region, and a summary. The tables are ready for a database or for statistical analysis: the clinical context (patient, position, side in park bench) is joined at the time of the analysis, the recording does not need to know it.

The definitions and the evidence are in notebooks/07_clinical_indices.ipynb (11 tidal recordings, four PEEP trials); on the four trials the functions below give the crossing PEEP, the best PEEP and the change of EELI in mL of the notebook.

Steps for a user: analyse a recording.

  1. Entry points
  2. Indices of a breath
  3. Tidal recordings
  4. PEEP trials
  5. Limits

docs.title: 1. Entry points
docs.text:
from fasteit.features import peep_trial_features, tidal_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext, Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

# A recording at one setting (or the tidal phase of a longer one).
recording = preprocess(load_data("patient01.bin"),
                       context=RecordingContext(tidal_volume_ml=450))  # Vt optional
tidal = tidal_features(recording)            # or phase=Segment(0, 300, category="phase", label="tidal")
tidal.breaths    # one row per breath
tidal.regions    # one row per breath and region
tidal.summary    # median and quartiles over the valid breaths, by region and index

# A PEEP trial.
context = RecordingContext(protocol="peep_trial", tidal_volume_ml=450)
trial = segment_peep_trial(preprocess(load_data("peep_trial.bin"), context=context))
features = peep_trial_features(trial)   # parameters in features.config (AnalysisConfig)
features.steps          # one row per PEEP step
features.step_regions   # one row per step and region
features.summary        # crossing PEEP, best PEEP, R/I (global and by region)

The object holds everything: features.trial.steps (driving pressure and tidal volume of each step, breaths analysed), features.trial.breaths (step of each breath), features.trial.recording.breaths (times, quality flags, PEEP, plateau, driving pressure, measured tidal volume). Each value is stored once: the tables of layer 3 have the keys (breath_id, step, peep, region) and what layer 3 computes, and are joined on the keys with the tables before them. The flat tables with everything in one row per breath and per step, for statistical analysis and databases, are made by layer 4 (export.md).

docs.title: 2. Indices of a breath
docs.text:
All from the frames of the layer 2 breath (one sample, no averaging): start = end-expiratory valley, peak = end-inspiratory peak.

Column Definition Source eeli signal inside the lung mask at the start of the breath (arbitrary units) TREND, Frerichs 2017, DOI: 10.1136/thoraxjnl-2016-208357 tiv signal at the peak minus at the start TREND gi global inhomogeneity: sum of |pixel TIV - median| / sum of pixel TIV, over the lung pixels Zhao 2009, DOI: 10.1007/s00134-009-1589-y cov_vd, cov_rl centre of ventilation on the image grid: 0 = ventral / patient right, 1 = dorsal / patient left Frerichs 2006, DOI: 10.1164/rccm.200512-1942OC respiratory_rate 60 / duration of the EIT breath (breaths/min) - tidal_volume_used, tidal_volume_source tidal volume used for the values in mL: typed for the step, typed for the recording, or measured layer 2 and 2b compliance TIV / driving pressure (EIT units per cmH2O) - compliance_ml tidal volume / driving pressure (mL/cmH2O): static compliance of the respiratory system, with the tidal volume typed or measured -

By region (regions, one row per breath and region; regions of layer 2: ventral and dorsal halves, layers, right and left, quadrants):

Column Definition eeli, tiv the same on the signal of the region share TIV of the region / TIV of the lung (0-1): a ratio of sums tiv_ml share × tidal volume (mL) compliance TIV of the region / driving pressure (EIT units per cmH2O): the sum of the compliances of its pixels, which are in parallel under the same driving pressure compliance_ml share × tidal volume / driving pressure (mL/cmH2O)

The two compliances are both kept: the one in mL/cmH2O is the static compliance of the respiratory system; the one in EIT units also follows what changes in the imaged slice (in volume control the same tidal volume gives 80-105 % of the TIV of the first step across a PEEP trial) and can move the best PEEP (B park bench: 4.5 in EIT units, 8.5 in mL/cmH2O). Costa is computed in EIT units only. A region's compliance is a partial compliance, its share of the total: a small region has a low compliance even when it is healthy.

docs.title: 3. Tidal recordings
docs.text: tidal_features(recording, phase=None) gives the indices of every breath, and a summary over the valid breaths (no quality flag, not excluded) inside the tidal phase (a breath is inside when it starts and ends inside it): one row per region ("global" for the whole lung) and index (feature), with median, q1, q3 and n_breaths (breaths with a value). The tidal volume of the breaths is the one typed in RecordingContext.tidal_volume_ml, otherwise the one measured on the ventilator curves.

docs.title: 4. PEEP trials
docs.text:
peep_trial_features(trial) gives the indices of every breath (with peep_step and analysed) and, for each step, from its analysed breaths:

Column Definition respiratory_rate, eeli, tiv, gi, cov_vd, cov_rl median of the analysed breaths compliance median TIV / driving pressure of the step: it also works when the driving pressure comes from one inspiratory hold or is typed compliance_ml tidal volume / driving pressure of the step (it needs no EIT data, so it exists also for a step without analysed breaths) compliance_pct_of_best, compliance_ml_pct_of_best as % of the best step collapse, overdistension Costa method (%), from the median tidal image of the step: pixel compliance, loss as % of the best of each pixel, weighted by the best compliance; the loss of a pixel is at most 100 % (Costa 2009, DOI: 10.1007/s00134-009-1447-y; formulas as in Shono and Kotani 2019, DOI: 10.1186/s40560-019-0358-4) d_eeli_tiv_vs_previous, d_eeli_tiv_vs_first change of EELI in tidal volumes: change / TIV of the step at the lower PEEP of the two (Wang 2020, DOI: 10.12659/MSM.922609) d_eeli_ml_vs_previous, d_eeli_ml_vs_first the same in mL: × tidal volume of that step d_compliance_pct_of_best_vs_..., d_compliance_ml_pct_of_best_vs_... changes of compliance vs the previous and the first step, in points of % of the best

Collapse and overdistension are read on their curves (one value per step); a change between two PEEP levels is the difference of two values of the curve.

step_regions has, for each step and region, the medians of eeli, tiv and share of the analysed breaths, and tiv_ml, compliance and compliance_ml of the step.

The summary is a long table (region, feature, value):

Feature Region Definition crossing_peep global PEEP where collapse and overdistension cross (linear interpolation; the lowest if they cross more than once) best_peep_compliance, best_peep_compliance_ml global PEEP of the best global compliance, in EIT units and in mL/cmH2O ri_peep_high, ri_peep_low global PEEP of the two steps used for R/I ri global and each region recruitment-to-inflation ratio recruited_volume_ml global and each region recruited volume (mL, with a tidal volume)

The PEEP of crossing_peep, the best PEEP and the R/I steps are on the levels of the protocol (peep_set, from SegmentationConfig.peep_levels) when every step has one, so that they can be compared between patients; otherwise on the measured PEEP. The R/I steps are chosen, and the drop of PEEP in its formula is computed, on the measured PEEP (the change of pressure that happened).

Recruitment-to-inflation ratio (Chen et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2020, DOI: 10.1164/rccm.201902-0334OC), between the step nearest to PEEP 15 and the step nearest to PEEP 5 at least 10 below it (AnalysisConfig):

dEELV = (EELI_high - EELI_low) x Vt_low / TIV_low        (Wang 2020)
recruited volume = dEELV - C_low x dPEEP                 C_low = Vt_low / driving_low
R/I = (recruited volume / dPEEP) / C_low = (EELI_high - EELI_low) / (C_EIT,low x dPEEP) - 1

The tidal volume cancels in R/I, which needs only EIT and the driving pressure; a region uses its own EELI and compliance. The original method reads one expiration after the drop of PEEP; here each level is the equilibrium EELI of a step, as in Wang 2020.

Steps with fewer analysed breaths than the minimum of layer 2b (enough false) are kept, with a warning: filter them in the analysis if needed. If the first step has no analysed breaths, the changes vs the first step are NaN.

docs.title: 5. Limits
docs.text:
• Tested on four decremental PEEP trials from two patients and on synthetic data with a known answer; Costa is implemented from its published formulas, not checked against another implementation.
  • EELI is in arbitrary units: only its changes count. Its change in mL assumes the same impedance per mL for the tidal and the end-expiratory change (Hinz et al., Intensive Care Med 2003, DOI: 10.1007/s00134-002-1555-4); in the four trials it was 1.6-2.3 times compliance × change of PEEP, cause unknown, so it is exploratory.
  • The mL of a region share the tidal volume as seen in the imaged slice: a distribution, not independent measurements.
  • Compliance is that of the respiratory system, in a passive patient; regional compliance uses the same driving pressure for every region.
  • % of the best step, Costa and the changes vs the first step depend on the PEEP range tested: compare patients with the same steps.
  • Costa reads an error common to a step (its driving pressure, the share of the tidal volume seen by the slice) as collapse or overdistension.
  • R/I mixes recruitment and overdistension (Zhao et al., Crit Care 2023, DOI: 10.1186/s13054-023-04520-8) and becomes large in a region almost collapsed at the low PEEP.
  • One lung mask for the whole recording: GI is not comparable with cut-offs computed on other masks.

Research use only - not a medical device.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install "fasteit @ git+https://github.com/Kernel236/fastEIT.git@v0.7.0a2"   # a fixed version
pip install git+https://github.com/Kernel236/fastEIT.git                        # the latest dev

Python 3.10 to 3.14. A study, or an app built on fastEIT, should install a fixed version: its results then do not change when the library does. The versions are listed on the tags page and in the version menu of this site.

For development (tests, linting) and to build this site:

git clone https://github.com/Kernel236/fastEIT.git
cd fastEIT
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"
mkdocs serve        # the site at http://127.0.0.1:8000/fastEIT/

docs.title: Supported files
docs.text:
The analysis starts from reconstructed images (32x32 pixels per frame):

File Read as Analysed Dräger PulmoVista 500 .bin ReconstructedFrameData (images and ventilator signals) yes Timpel .csv, .txt, .asc export ReconstructedFrameData yes Dräger .eit RawImpedanceData (208 raw measurements per frame) no: needs a reconstruction first Dräger .asc export ContinuousSignalData (signals only) no: no images

load_data(path) recognises the vendor and the format by itself. Large .bin and .eit files are not read into memory at once: the images and measurements are read from disk when they are used.

docs.title: The four steps
docs.text:
from fasteit.export import recording_tables, write_csv
from fasteit.features import tidal_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess

raw = load_data("recording.bin")                                   # 1. read the file
recording = preprocess(raw, context=RecordingContext(patient_id="P01", label="T0"))  # 2. breaths
features = tidal_features(recording)                               # 3. clinical indices
write_csv(recording_tables(features), "results/")                  # 4. tables for statistical analysis

Each step returns an object that keeps the one before it, with a log of what was done. A PEEP trial adds one step (segment_peep_trial) between 2 and 3. The user guide goes through the steps: analyse a recording (both protocols), cut a recording, review figures and export the tables. How each layer works is under "How it works" (data model).

Research use only - not a medical device.

docs.title: fastEIT - Parser Reference
docs.text:
Specifications for all parsers: input formats, output containers, calibration details, and the pyEIT reconstruction bridge.

For data container field specifications see data_model.md. For architecture and extension recipes see parsing_layer.md.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
File Vendor Parser Container .bin Dräger DragerBinParser ReconstructedFrameData .asc / .txt / .csv Dräger DragerAscParser ContinuousSignalData .eit Dräger DragerEitParser RawImpedanceData .csv / .txt / .asc Timpel TimpelTabularParser ReconstructedFrameData

All parsers inherit from BaseParser and are accessible via load_data(path).

docs.title: 2. DragerBinParser - .bin
docs.text:
File: parsers/draeger/bin/bin_parser.py

Reads vendor-reconstructed 32×32 pixel frames exported by the PulmoVista 500. Two frame formats are registered; detection is size-based (no header).

docs.title: Frame formats
docs.text: Name Frame size Medibus channels Notes Draeger_base_4358 4358 bytes 52 Standard export Draeger_ext_4382 4382 bytes 58 BiLevel parameters + 4 PressurePod channels; the channels are there whether or not a Pod is connected, metadata["has_pressure_pod"] says if they hold values

docs.title: Binary frame layout (base format)
docs.text:
Field Type Size Content ts float64 8 B Wall-clock timestamp as fraction of day (kept as-is; × 86400 gives seconds) dummy float32 4 B Unknown - ignored pixels float32 × 1024 4096 B Reconstructed 32×32 image (C-order) min_max_flag int32 4 B +1 = inspiratory peak, −1 = expiratory trough, 0 = none event_marker int32 4 B Event counter event_text S30 30 B ASCII event label, padded with spaces (or nulls on frames without an event) timing_error int32 4 B 0 = frame timing OK medibus_data float32 × 52 208 B Ventilator Medibus channels; sentinel −3.4×10³⁸ = disconnected

The two formats share Medibus indices 0-50 and differ from index 51 onward:

Index Base (52 channels) PressurePod (58 channels) 51 time_at_low_pressure high_pressure (BiLevel PHigh) 52 - low_pressure (BiLevel Plow) 53 - time_at_low_pressure (BiLevel Tlow) 54-57 - Pod waveforms: airway_pressure_pod, esophageal_pressure_pod, transpulmonary_pressure_pod, gastric_pressure_pod

Full field list with units: parsers/draeger/bin/draeger_dtypes.py.

docs.title: Sentinel values
docs.text: Disconnected Medibus channels carry the sentinel −3.4×10³⁸ (IEEE 754 bit pattern 0xFF7FC99E); BiLevel fields (51-53 in the PressurePod format) read −1000.0 when the ventilator is not in BiLevel mode. The parser returns these values unchanged. Replacing them with NaN is a preprocessing step; bin_utils.replace_no_data_sentinels() is available for it.

docs.title: Sampling frequency
docs.text: Not stored in the binary. Estimated from the timestamps: fs = (N − 1) / (t_last − t_first), with timestamps converted to seconds and unwrapped across midnight, rounded to the nearest integer Hz. Falls back to 50 Hz (recorded in metadata["warnings"]) when the estimate fails.

docs.title: 3. DragerEitParser - .eit
docs.text:
File: parsers/draeger/eit/eit_parser.py

Reads raw transimpedance measurements from the PulmoVista 500 proprietary binary format. We are not aware of another open-source Python parser for it.

docs.title: File structure
docs.text:
Bytes 0-11          : preamble - 3 × int32 LE
                        [0:4]  format_version (always 51)
                        [4:8]  sep_offset      (file-specific, variable)
                        [8:12] unknown_int
Bytes 12-sep_offset : ASCII header ("key: value\r\n" lines, latin-1)
Bytes sep_offset-+7 : separator b'**\r\n\r\n\r\n' (8 bytes)
Bytes sep_offset+8… : binary frames, 5495 bytes each

docs.title: ASCII header fields
docs.text: Header key Metadata key Type Notes Framerate [Hz] fs float Acquisition rate (typically 50.0 Hz) Date date str DD.MM.YYYY Time time str HH:MM:SS.mmm Frequency [kHz] frequency_khz float Excitation frequency (≈101.5 kHz) Amplitude [uA] amplitude_ua float Injection current amplitude (≈9100 µA) Gain gain int Hardware amplifier gain Samples samples_per_period int ADC samples per excitation period Periods periods int Excitation periods per measurement

docs.title: Binary frame layout (5495 bytes)
docs.text: Field Type Size Content timestamp float64 8 B Fraction of day unknown_f8 float64 8 B Unknown trans_A float64 × 208 1664 B Primary transimpedance set (ADC counts) unknown_16a float64 × 16 128 B Unknown injection_current float64 × 16 128 B Injected current per drive pattern (ADC counts) unknown_16b float64 × 16 128 B Unknown voltage_A float64 × 16 128 B Electrode voltage A (ADC counts) unknown_50 float64 × 50 400 B Unknown trans_B float64 × 208 1664 B Reference transimpedance set (ADC counts) unknown_48 float64 × 48 384 B Unknown voltage_B float64 × 16 128 B Electrode voltage B (ADC counts) unknown_6 float64 × 6 48 B Unknown gugus float64 × 44 352 B Ignored (EIDORS terminology) unknown_byte uint8 1 B Unknown medibus float32 × 67 268 B Ventilator Medibus channels (67 in .eit, 52 in .bin) event_text S30 30 B ASCII event label mixed uint8 × 24 24 B Mixed content frame_counter uint16 2 B Rolling frame counter padding uint8 × 2 2 B Alignment padding

docs.title: Calibration pipeline
docs.text:
Empirical constants from EIDORS read_draeger_file.m (A. Adler, estimated 2016-04-07). These are not present in the .eit header - they are hardware-specific and hardcoded.

Constant Value Role FT_A 0.00098242 Transimpedance scaling - primary channel FT_B 0.00019607 Transimpedance scaling - reference channel FC_CURRENT 194326.3536 ADC counts → Ampere FV_VOLTAGE 0.11771 ADC counts → Volt 
vv      = FT_A * trans_A - FT_B * trans_B   # (N_frames, 208) calibrated transimpedance [Ω]
I_real  = injection_current / FC_CURRENT     # (N_frames, 16)  injected current [A]
V_diff  = (voltage_A - voltage_B) / FV_VOLTAGE  # (N_frames, 16) differential voltage [V]

docs.title: Measurement protocol
docs.text: 208 measurements per frame = 16 electrodes × 13 measurement pairs. Adjacent current injection (drive distance = 1 electrode), adjacent voltage measurement (step = 1 electrode).

docs.title: 4. DragerAscParser - .asc
docs.text:
File: parsers/draeger/asc/asc_parser.py

Reads the PulmoVista 500 continuous waveform export (tab-separated text). Returns ContinuousSignalData with one row per EIT frame.

Detection: looks for the DraegerEIT Software header string in the first 40 lines (read as latin-1). Sampling frequency is estimated from the time column (fraction of day) when present, otherwise fs is None.

Typical columns: image, time, global, local_1_x_16_y_29 … local_4_x_16_y_05, minmax, event, eventtext, timing_error, plus Medibus channel columns when the ventilator is connected via Medibus.

docs.title: 5. TimpelTabularParser - .csv / .txt / .asc
docs.text:
File: parsers/timpel/timpel_parser.py

Reads Timpel EIT device tabular exports. Each row is one EIT frame; columns 0-1023 are the 32×32 pixel values (C-order); columns 1024-1029 are auxiliary signals (airway_pressure, flow, volume, min_flag, max_flag, qrs_flag).

Returns ReconstructedFrameData. The export has no timestamp column, so fs is fixed at 50 Hz and ts is generated as (frame_index + first_frame) / 50.

Detection: the keyword timpel in the first 40 lines, or a first data row with at least 1029 separators (comma, tab or semicolon), i.e. the 1030-column layout.

docs.title: 6. GREIT reconstruction bridge
docs.text:
This function is far from reliable. It was written only to show one possible application of the .eit parser output: passing it to a reconstruction library such as pyEIT.

File: parsers/draeger/eit/eit_pyeit_bridge.py Optional dependency: pip install fasteit[pyeit]

Converts RawImpedanceData.measurements (N_frames, 208) to reconstructed 32×32 images (N_frames, 32, 32) using the GREIT algorithm.

Reference: Adler A et al., "GREIT: a unified approach to 2D linear EIT reconstruction of lung images." Physiol. Meas. 30 (2009) S35-S55. DOI: 10.1088/0967-3334/30/6/S03

docs.title: build_greit(n_el, h0, p, lamb, n) → (solver, protocol)
docs.text:
Builds a pyEIT GREIT solver on a circular unit-disk mesh.

Parameter Default Meaning n_el 16 Number of electrodes h0 0.1 Mesh density p 0.2 GREIT noise figure (Adler 2009 recommendation) lamb 1e-2 Tikhonov regularisation n 32 Output image side length in pixels

docs.title: reconstruct_greit(measurements, ref_frame, …) → ndarray
docs.text:
ref_frame value Behaviour None Mean of all frames in this recording (default) int Single frame index (start, end) Mean of measurements[start:end] np.ndarray (208,) External reference - for cross-recording EELI comparison

Sign convention: GREIT outputs conductivity change (Δσ); the function negates it to match the Dräger impedance convention (air → impedance rises → positive peak).

Image orientation - three steps applied inside reconstruct_greit(), all sourced from PulmoVista 500 IFU SW 1.3n: 1. Negate (sign flip): impedance convention - see above. 2. rot90(k=1) (90° CCW): electrode 1 sits at 12 o'clock on the PulmoVista belt (anterior/ventral wall); pyEIT places electrode 0 at 3 o'clock. Rotation moves the anterior region to the top of the image. Source: IFU p. 144. 3. fliplr (horizontal mirror): Dräger displays images in caudal-cranial projection (CT convention viewed from feet): left side of image = right side of patient. pyEIT produces the anatomical mirror; fliplr corrects this. Source: IFU p. 146.

Spatial quality note: a generic circular mesh does not replicate Dräger's proprietary reconstruction. Both algorithms produce correct relative distributions, but the vendor .bin uses a device-specific mesh and matrix.

docs.title: 7. Loader utilities
docs.text: File: parsers/loader.py

docs.title: load_data(path) → BaseData
docs.text:
Single entry point. Auto-detects vendor and format, selects the right parser, returns the appropriate container. Raises ValueError for an unsupported extension or unrecognised content, NotImplementedError when no parser is registered for the detected vendor/extension, and a ParserError subclass for .bin files with an unknown or ambiguous frame size.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data

data = load_data("patient01.bin")   # → ReconstructedFrameData
data = load_data("patient01.eit")   # → RawImpedanceData
data = load_data("patient01.asc")   # → ContinuousSignalData

docs.title: load_many(paths) → list[BaseData]
docs.text:
Parses an explicit list of paths in order. Formats can be mixed.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_many

recordings = load_many(["patient01.bin", "patient02.bin", "patient01.asc"])

docs.title: load_folder(folder, pattern="*") → list[BaseData]
docs.text:
Scans a directory, parses every file with a registered parser. Files that raise an error are skipped and a one-line message is printed to stderr.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_folder

all_bin  = load_folder("/data/session01/", pattern="*.bin")
all_data = load_folder("/data/session01/")          # mixed formats
recursive = load_folder("/data/", pattern="**/*.bin")

docs.title: fastEIT - Parsing Layer: How It Works and How to Extend It
docs.text:
This document explains the architecture of the parsing layer and provides step-by-step recipes for the most common extension tasks:

  1. How the parsing layer works
  2. Add a new Dräger .bin frame size
  3. Add a new parser
  4. Testing checklist
  5. File layout

docs.title: The single entry point
docs.text:
Everything starts from load_data(path) in parsers/loader.py. You call it with a file path; it returns the right data container without you knowing which parser was used.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data

data = load_data("patient01.bin")   # → ReconstructedFrameData
data = load_data("patient01.asc")   # → ContinuousSignalData

Internally it does three things in sequence:

1. detect_vendor_and_format(path)   ← What file is this?
2. build_parser_from_detection(...)  ← Which parser handles it?
3. parser.parse_safe(path)           ← Read and return data

docs.title: Detection (parsers/detection.py)
docs.text:
Detection maps a file to (vendor, extension, optional_bin_format). The strategy depends on the extension:

Extension Strategy How it works .bin size-based file_size % frame_size == 0 for each registered FormatSpec .eit header-based reads first bytes, looks for ASCII magic string for each registered HeaderFormatSpec .asc .txt .csv content-based reads first 40 lines, looks for a vendor keyword; Timpel is also recognised by its 1030-column row

.bin is special: there is no header. The only way to identify the format is that the file size must be an exact multiple of the frame size in bytes. The BIN_FORMAT_SPECS list in parsers/bin_formats.py holds every known frame size. If only one spec matches → that's the format. If zero match → error. If more than one match → AmbiguousFormatError (rare, requires two frame sizes that divide the same file size).

docs.title: Parser registry (parsers/loader.py)
docs.text:
default_parser_registry() returns a plain dict:

{
    ("draeger", ".bin"): lambda: DragerBinParser(),
    ("draeger", ".eit"): lambda: DragerEitParser(),
    ("draeger", ".asc"): lambda: DragerAscParser(),
    ("draeger", ".txt"): lambda: DragerAscParser(),
    ("draeger", ".csv"): lambda: DragerAscParser(),
    ("timpel",  ".csv"): lambda: TimpelTabularParser(),
    ("timpel",  ".txt"): lambda: TimpelTabularParser(),
    ("timpel",  ".asc"): lambda: TimpelTabularParser(),
}

Key = (vendor_lowercase, extension_with_dot_lowercase). Value = zero-argument factory that returns a fresh parser instance.

docs.title: BaseParser and parse_safe
docs.text:
Every parser inherits from BaseParser (Template Method pattern):

BaseParser
  ├── validate(path) → bool        ← you implement this
  ├── parse(path) → BaseData       ← you implement this
  └── parse_safe(path) → BaseData  ← free: validates then parses

parse_safe raises FileNotFoundError if the file is missing and ValueError if validate() returns False. Callers always use parse_safe (or load_data, which calls it). Direct parse() skips validation and is used internally or in tests.

docs.title: Data flow summary
docs.text:
load_data("patient01.bin")
    │
    ├─ detect_vendor_and_format()
    │   └─ file_size 4358000 % 4358 == 0
    │       → FormatSpec("Draeger_base_4358", vendor="draeger", frame_size=4358)
    │       → FileDetection(extension=".bin", vendor="draeger", bin_format=spec)
    │
    ├─ build_parser_from_detection()
    │   └─ registry[("draeger", ".bin")] → DragerBinParser()
    │
    ├─ parser.parse_safe("patient01.bin")
    │   ├─ validate() → file exists, size divisible by known frame size → True
    │   └─ parse()
    │       ├─ np.memmap with spec.dtype
    │       ├─ fs estimation from timestamps
    │       └─ ReconstructedFrameData(frames, aux_signals, fs, ...)
    │
    └─ attach detected vendor/extension to data.metadata
       return ReconstructedFrameData

docs.title: Multi-file loaders
docs.text:
Two convenience wrappers built on top of load_data():

load_many(paths) - takes an explicit list of paths, returns a list of BaseData in the same order. Vendor and format can be mixed freely.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_many

recordings = load_many([
    "patient01.bin",
    "patient02.bin",
    "patient01.asc",
])

load_folder(folder, pattern="*") - scans a directory (alphabetically), parses every file that has a registered parser, and skips files that raise an error (no registered parser, malformed file, wrong extension). Each skipped file prints a one-line message to stderr; the scan is never aborted.

from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_folder

# All files in a folder (mixed formats)
recordings = load_folder("/data/session01/")

# Only .bin files
recordings = load_folder("/data/session01/", pattern="*.bin")

# Recursive search
recordings = load_folder("/data/", pattern="**/*.bin")

Both functions accept the same optional registry= argument as load_data(), making it easy to inject a custom parser registry for testing or for formats not yet registered by default.

docs.title: 2. Add a new Dräger .bin frame size
docs.text:
If a new PulmoVista firmware introduces a new frame layout (e.g., 4406 bytes with 6 additional Medibus fields).

Files to change: 2. Everything else is automatic.

docs.title: Step 1 - Define the dtype
docs.text:
File: src/fasteit/parsers/draeger/bin/draeger_dtypes.py

Add the new structured dtype and field list following the existing pattern. The layout must sum exactly to the new frame size - verify with a comment.

# New extended frame (4406 bytes) - hypothetical example
FRAME_NEWEXT_DTYPE = np.dtype([
    ("ts",           "<f8"),          #   8 bytes
    ("dummy",        "<f4"),          #   4 bytes
    ("pixels",       "<f4", (32, 32)),# 4096 bytes
    ("min_max_flag", "<i4"),          #   4 bytes
    ("event_marker", "<i4"),          #   4 bytes
    ("event_text",   "S30"),          #  30 bytes
    ("timing_error", "<i4"),          #   4 bytes
    ("medibus_data", "<f4", (64,)),   # 256 bytes  ← was 208 or 232
])
# Total: 8+4+4096+4+4+30+4+256 = 4406 bytes

MEDIBUS_NEWEXT_FIELDS: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = _MEDIBUS_COMMON + [
    # idx 51: first new field
    ("high_pressure", "mbar", False),
    # idx 52-63: remaining new fields ...
]

MEDIBUS_NEWEXT_INDEX: dict[str, int] = {
    name: i for i, (name, _, _) in enumerate(MEDIBUS_NEWEXT_FIELDS)
}

Rule: the frame layout must be byte-exact. Add the arithmetic comment (# Total: ...) and verify it matches the new frame size before continuing.

docs.title: Step 2 - Register the format spec
docs.text:
File: src/fasteit/parsers/bin_formats.py

from fasteit.parsers.draeger.bin.draeger_dtypes import (
    FRAME_NEWEXT_DTYPE,
    MEDIBUS_NEWEXT_FIELDS,
)

BIN_FORMAT_SPECS: tuple[FormatSpec, ...] = (
    FormatSpec(
        name="Draeger_base_4358",
        ...
    ),
    FormatSpec(
        name="Draeger_ext_4382",
        ...
    ),
    FormatSpec(                                      # ← add this
        name="Draeger_newext_4406",
        vendor="draeger",
        frame_size_bytes=4406,
        dtype=FRAME_NEWEXT_DTYPE,
        medibus_fields=tuple(name for name, _, _ in MEDIBUS_NEWEXT_FIELDS),
    ),
)

That's it. detect_bin_format_from_size() picks it up automatically. DragerBinParser.parse() uses spec.dtype and spec.medibus_fields from the spec - no parser changes needed.

docs.title: 3. Add a new parser
docs.text:
This recipe covers any combination: new vendor or existing vendor, binary or tabular. The five steps are always the same; only the content of steps 1 and 2 differs by format type.

Return type by format:

Format Return type Example Binary frame sequence ReconstructedFrameData Dräger .bin, AcmEIT .acm Tabular (CSV / TXT), signals only ContinuousSignalData Dräger .asc, Hamilton export, SERVO-U export, capnograph Tabular with pixel columns ReconstructedFrameData Timpel .csv

Tabular parsers are common for any device that exports to a plain-text table - including standalone ventilators (Hamilton, Maquet SERVO, Dräger Evita) that export continuous waveforms (Flow, Paw, Volume) and/or breath-averaged parameters (TV, RR, PEEP, compliance) in the same file.

Files to change: 4-5.

docs.title: Step 1 - Detection
docs.text:
Detection works the same way for all three file families: register a spec, the generic function finds it automatically. You rarely need to touch detection.py.

.eit-style (header + binary frames, same .eit extension, new vendor)

File: src/fasteit/parsers/header_formats.py

Just add a HeaderFormatSpec and append it to HEADER_FORMAT_SPECS. detect_vendor_from_eit_header() iterates the list and returns the first match - no changes to detection.py needed.

CAREFUSION_EIT_SPEC = HeaderFormatSpec(
    name="Carefusion_EIT_v1",
    vendor="carefusion",
    magic_string="CareFusion",      # ASCII substring in first magic_search_bytes bytes
    magic_search_bytes=256,
    encoding="utf-8",
    frame_size_bytes=5120,          # byte-exact frame size for this firmware
    n_electrodes=16,
    n_measurements=208,
)

HEADER_FORMAT_SPECS: tuple[HeaderFormatSpec, ...] = (
    DRAEGER_EIT_HEADER_SPEC,
    CAREFUSION_EIT_SPEC,            # ← add here; detection is automatic
)

HeaderFormatSpec fields:

Field Purpose magic_string ASCII substring searched in the first magic_search_bytes magic_search_bytes How many bytes to read for detection (keep it small) encoding Header text encoding (usually "latin-1" or "utf-8") frame_size_bytes Byte-exact size of one binary frame - used by the parser n_electrodes / n_measurements Protocol geometry metadata

.eit-style but with a new extension (e.g. .acm)

Add one branch in detect_vendor_and_format() that calls the same generic detect_vendor_from_eit_header() (if the magic-string approach works for this format):

# In detect_vendor_and_format() - detection.py:
if extension == ".acm":
    vendor = detect_vendor_from_eit_header(path)  # reuses HEADER_FORMAT_SPECS
    return FileDetection(path=path, extension=extension, vendor=vendor)

Then add the HeaderFormatSpec to HEADER_FORMAT_SPECS as above.

Binary without a header (size-based, .bin)

Add a FormatSpec to BIN_FORMAT_SPECS (see section 2). No changes to detection.py needed.

Tabular (CSV / TXT / ASC)

File: src/fasteit/parsers/detection.py - extend detect_vendor_from_tabular() with a keyword found in the first 40 lines:

# In detect_vendor_from_tabular():
if "hamilton medical" in normalized:
    return "hamilton"

docs.title: Step 2 - Schema definition
docs.text:
Binary - define a numpy structured dtype (byte-exact) and a Medibus-style field list. File: src/fasteit/parsers/acmeit/acmeit_dtypes.py (new)

import numpy as np

ACMEIT_FRAME_DTYPE = np.dtype([
    ("ts",     "<f8"),           #    8 bytes
    ("pixels", "<f4", (32, 32)), # 4096 bytes
    ("flow",   "<f4"),           #    4 bytes
    ("paw",    "<f4"),           #    4 bytes
])
# Total: 8 + 4096 + 4 + 4 = 4112 bytes

Tabular - define a (snake_case_name, unit, is_continuous) field list. (Optional but recommended - makes the schema self-documenting and testable.) File: src/fasteit/parsers/hamilton/hamilton_dtypes.py (new)

HAMILTON_FIELDS: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = [
    ("flow",             "L/min", True),   # continuous waveform
    ("airway_pressure",  "mbar",  True),   # continuous waveform
    ("volume",           "mL",    True),   # continuous waveform
    ("respiratory_rate", "/min",  False),  # breath-averaged
    ("tidal_volume",     "mL",    False),  # breath-averaged
    ("peep",             "mbar",  False),  # breath-averaged
]

The is_continuous flag lets downstream code select only waveforms or only breath-averaged values without touching the parser.

docs.title: Step 3 - Parser class
docs.text:
File: src/fasteit/parsers/<vendor>/<vendor>_parser.py (new)

The structure is always the same: validate() + parse().

Binary parser:

from pathlib import Path
from fasteit.models.reconstructed_data import ReconstructedFrameData
from fasteit.parsers.base import BaseParser

class AcmEitParser(BaseParser):

    def validate(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        path = Path(path)
        if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
            return False
        # e.g. check magic bytes or frame-size divisibility
        return True

    def parse(self, path: Path) -> ReconstructedFrameData:
        # np.memmap with ACMEIT_FRAME_DTYPE, fs estimation ...
        # (keep sentinel values as-is: NaN replacement belongs to preprocessing)
        return ReconstructedFrameData(
            frames=frames,
            aux_signals=aux_signals,
            fs=fs,
            filename=str(path),
            file_format="acm",
        )

Tabular parser:

import io
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
from fasteit.models.continuous_data import ContinuousSignalData
from fasteit.parsers.base import BaseParser
from fasteit.parsers.detection import detect_vendor_from_tabular

class HamiltonParser(BaseParser):

    def validate(self, path: Path) -> bool:
        path = Path(path)
        if not path.exists() or path.stat().st_size == 0:
            return False
        try:
            return detect_vendor_from_tabular(path) == "hamilton"
        except ValueError:
            return False

    def parse(self, path: Path) -> ContinuousSignalData:
        path = Path(path)
        with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            lines = f.readlines()

        # Locate the column-header row (skip any prose header above it)
        header_idx = next(
            i for i, l in enumerate(lines)
            if l.strip().startswith("Time")  # adapt to real format
        )
        df = pd.read_csv(
            io.StringIO("".join(lines[header_idx:])),
            sep=";",            # or "\t" - check the real file
            decimal=",",
            na_values=["-", "---"],
            index_col=False,
        )
        df.columns = [c.strip().lower().replace(" ", "_") for c in df.columns]

        fs = None
        if "time" in df.columns:
            dt = pd.to_numeric(df["time"], errors="coerce").diff().dropna().median()
            if pd.notna(dt) and dt > 0:
                fs = round(1.0 / float(dt))  # time assumed already in seconds

        return ContinuousSignalData(
            table=df,
            fs=fs,
            filename=str(path),
            file_format=path.suffix.lstrip("."),
            metadata={"parsed_section": "ventilator_export"},
        )

docs.title: Step 4 - Register in loader
docs.text:
File: src/fasteit/parsers/loader.py

from fasteit.parsers.hamilton.hamilton_parser import HamiltonParser   # or AcmEitParser

def default_parser_registry():
    return {
        ...
        ("hamilton", ".csv"): lambda: HamiltonParser(),
        ("hamilton", ".txt"): lambda: HamiltonParser(),
    }

Registry key = (vendor_lowercase, extension_with_dot). If a vendor uses multiple extensions for the same format, add one entry per extension pointing to the same parser factory.

docs.title: Step 5 - Export from package __init__
docs.text:
File: src/fasteit/parsers/__init__.py

from fasteit.parsers.hamilton.hamilton_parser import HamiltonParser
__all__ = [..., "HamiltonParser"]

docs.title: Note: same extension, different vendors
docs.text: If two vendors share the same extension (e.g. both export .csv), detect_vendor_from_tabular() reads the file content and returns a different vendor string for each. The registry key (vendor, extension) ensures the correct parser is called.

docs.title: 4. Testing checklist
docs.text:
Every new parser must have tests before it is considered done. Minimal coverage for a tabular parser:

  • [ ] test_validate_returns_true_on_valid_file - synthetic file, happy path
  • [ ] test_validate_returns_false_on_wrong_extension - wrong extension
  • [ ] test_validate_returns_false_on_wrong_vendor_keyword - wrong content
  • [ ] test_parse_returns_continuous_signal_data - correct type and file_format
  • [ ] test_parse_fs_estimated - fs is a reasonable integer (e.g. 50)
  • [ ] test_parse_column_names_normalised - no spaces or special characters
  • [ ] test_parse_time_column_present - "time" in data.table.columns
  • [ ] test_parse_continuous_channels_present - at least one signal channel
  • [ ] test_parse_raises_on_missing_table_section - ValueError on malformed file
  • [ ] test_load_data_routes_to_parser - load_data(path).vendor == "myvendor"

docs.title: fastEIT - Preprocessing Layer
docs.text:
The preprocessing layer (layer 2) takes one parsed recording with pixels (ReconstructedFrameData: a Dräger .bin or a Timpel export) and returns an EITRecording ready for breath-by-breath analysis. A Dräger .eit (raw measurements) needs a reconstruction first; a Dräger .asc has no images. It is the same for every protocol (tidal breathing, PEEP trial): each breath gets its EIT timings and quality, and its ventilator values (PEEP, plateau, driving pressure, tidal volume). The segmentation by protocol and the clinical indices (EELI, TIV, GI, CoV, compliance) come in the next layers.

The evidence for every choice is in notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb (11 real recordings); for the pressures of each breath, in notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb (four PEEP trials). The EIT steps reimplement eitprocessing v1.8.8 (Somhorst et al., JOSS 2026;11(117):8179, DOI: 10.21105/joss.08179) and the tests check them against it.

  1. Entry point
  2. Steps
  3. Ventilator values of each breath
  4. Output
  5. Logs
  6. Limits
  7. File layout

docs.title: 1. Entry point
docs.text:
from fasteit.config import PreprocessingConfig
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext, Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess

raw = load_data("patient01.bin")
recording = preprocess(
    raw,                                             # never modified
    config=PreprocessingConfig(heart_rate_bpm=85),   # the choices of a study, with their source
    exclusions=[Segment(120, 180, label="cough")],   # parts chosen by the user
    context=RecordingContext(
        patient_id="PZ01",
        protocol="tidal",
        tidal_volume_ml=450,                         # optional: e.g. set in volume control
    ),
)

The same inputs always give the same output, so an application only needs to store the inputs (file, config, exclusions, context) and can recompute the rest. PreprocessingConfig is frozen: to change a parameter make a new one, e.g. dataclasses.replace(config, heart_rate_bpm=80). It holds the choices a study may change (heart rate, quality flags, lung mask threshold, exclusion margin); the details of the methods taken from eitprocessing or fixed by the evidence are constants of their modules, with their source.

docs.title: 2. Steps
docs.text:
# Step Module Source 1 Time in seconds, pixels copied with the Dräger "no data" values as NaN pipeline - 2 Device exclusions: frames with missing pixels (filled with the nearest frame), timing errors, gaps in the frame times exclusions - 3 Respiratory rate from the Welch spectrum cardiac_filter eitprocessing RateDetection 4 Cardiac step: MDN filter if the user gives the heart rate, otherwise a 0.1 s moving average (the heart is not removed) cardiac_filter Wisse et al., Physiol Meas 2024, DOI: 10.1088/1361-6579/ad46e3 5 Breath detection on the sum of all pixels: valley, peak, next valley breaths eitprocessing BreathDetection 6 Quality flags and exclusions of each breath; is_valid = no flag and not excluded breath_quality, exclusions notebook 05 §8 7 Lung mask from the valid breaths: watershed of the TIV and amplitude maps at 15 % of the maximum TIV, islands < 10 pixels removed lung_mask eitprocessing WatershedLungspace, FilterROIBySize 8 Regions of interest inside the mask and their signals regions notebook 05 §9 9 Auxiliary signals (pressures, flow, volume, device breath markers): "no data" values as NaN, channels without data left out, not filtered, the same units for every vendor auxiliary - 10 Airway pressures of each breath: PEEP, plateau, driving pressure breath_pressures notebook 06 §2, §4 11 Inspiratory tidal volume of each breath tidal_volume -

Breaths are flagged, never removed: the clinician decides what to use. Every exclusion is widened by 0.5 s on each side (exclusion_margin_seconds) and a breath that touches it is excluded. In the later layers a breath belongs to a phase or a PEEP step when it starts and ends inside it. The user-facing rules are in cut a recording.

Quality flags of each breath:

Column Rule flag_short, flag_long duration below 0.5 s or above 20 s flag_suspect_ti_ratio Ti/Ttot (from impedance) outside 0.2-0.6 flag_amplitude_outlier amplitude below 0.5× or above 2× the median of the 21 surrounding breaths flag_duration_outlier duration above 2× the median of the 21 surrounding breaths flag_invalid_data within 0.5 s of a gross outlier of the signal

docs.title: 3. Ventilator values of each breath
docs.text:
The auxiliary signals get the same units for every vendor, once, in auxiliary:

Quantity Unit From Pressures (airway, oesophageal, PEEP, plateau...) cmH2O Dräger mbar × 1.0197 (1 mbar = 100 Pa, 1 cmH2O = 98.0665 Pa); Timpel already cmH2O Flow L/s Dräger Medibus L/min ÷ 60; Timpel already L/s Volumes mL Timpel L × 1000; Dräger already mL (two Medibus values in L) Derived values e.g. mL/cmH2O, cmH2O/L/s Medibus compliance, resistance, elastance

Minute volumes stay in L/min. EITRecording.aux_units gives the unit of each column.

Then each breath gets, in the breath table, the first source available:

Columns Source, in order of preference Channel used peep, plateau, driving_pressure (cmH2O) 1. airway pressure waveform: Dräger PressurePod, then Medibus or Timpel airway_pressure; 2. without a waveform, the PEEP and plateau computed by the ventilator (Medibus), median over the breath pressure_channel tidal_volume (mL, inspiratory) 1. volume curve: highest volume around the inspiration minus the lowest before it; 2. integral of the inspiratory flow; 3. the tidal volume computed by the ventilator (Medibus: mandatory, then spontaneous inspiratory value, then the generic "tidal volume"), median over the breath tidal_volume_channel

The pressures are all read on the same channel, so that a constant offset of the sensor cancels in the driving pressure:

  • start of inspiration: the last minimum of the pressure before its steepest rise, searched near the EIT valley;
  • PEEP: the median pressure in the 0.2 s before it;
  • plateau: the median pressure from 0.25 to 0.05 s before the start of expiration, only after an end-inspiratory hold of at least 0.5 s. In pressure control the flat inspiratory pressure is read the same way;
  • driving pressure = plateau - PEEP. The peak pressure is never used instead.

The tidal volume is read in a window from half an expiration before the EIT breath (but not before the middle of the expiration before) to the middle of its own expiration, so that it holds the whole inspiration even when the EIT valley falls a little after the start of the inspiratory flow, and nothing of the inspirations around it. On the flow curve only the run of inspiratory flow around its peak is integrated, so that noise and cardiac oscillations around zero flow are not counted. In volume control it is the volume delivered, the one set on the ventilator. If the flow does not rise during the EIT inspiration of most breaths (inspiration recorded as negative), the log gives a warning.

A tidal volume typed by the user for the whole recording goes in RecordingContext.tidal_volume_ml: the volume set in volume control, or the mean on the case report form, only when it is the same for the whole recording (in pressure control it changes with PEEP: type it per step, segmentation.md). It is kept apart from the measured one: the next layers use the typed one first. A typed volume outside 100-1500 mL gives a warning (litres typed instead of mL?).

docs.title: 4. Output
docs.text:
EITRecording fields:

Field Content raw, config, context the inputs exclusions manual and device exclusions, widened by 0.5 s and merged time seconds from the start of the recording rates, cardiac_filter respiratory rate, heart rate as entered, filter actually applied ("mdn" or "moving_average") pixels (N, 32, 32) float32 after the cardiac step image_mask pixels with a signal, wider than the lung detection_signal sum of all pixels: the breaths are its valleys and peaks global_signal sum of the pixels inside the lung mask breaths one row per breath: times and frames, flags, excluded, exclusion_label, is_valid, peep, plateau, driving_pressure, tidal_volume lung_mask, tiv_map ventilated lung and the mean TIV map it comes from roi_masks, roi_signals ventral, dorsal, right, left, layer_1-layer_4, four quadrants, cut on the ventilated lung (indices of a shift of ventilation use image coordinates) aux, aux_units auxiliary signals with data, one row per frame (e.g. airway_pressure_pod, esophageal_pressure_pod, Medibus peep, min_max_flag), and the unit of each pressure_channel, tidal_volume_channel the columns of aux the ventilator values of the breaths come from (None if none) log what each step did: checks passed, facts, warnings (section 5)

Images are seen from the feet, like a CT slice: row 0 is ventral, column 0 is the patient's right.

Breath frames index every signal of the same length, for example the pressure at the start and at the peak of a breath:

breath = recording.valid_breaths.iloc[0]
paw = recording.aux.airway_pressure_pod[[breath.start_idx, breath.peak_idx]]

The TIV image of one breath is its pixels at the peak minus at the start; tiv_map is the mean of these images over the valid breaths. To look at one breath, e.g. a suspected artefact:

from fasteit.preprocessing.lung_mask import breath_tiv_map

image = breath_tiv_map(recording, breath.breath_id)  # (32, 32)

docs.title: 5. Logs
docs.text:
There are two kinds of record, kept apart on purpose:

  • EITRecording.log belongs to the result: it says which filter ran, what was excluded and every warning, and is saved with the data. Each message has a level: OK: for a check that passed (no missing frames, respiratory rate inside the searched range, heart rate away from it, pressure and volume read, every region with lung pixels), no prefix for a fact (counts, sources), WARNING: for a check that failed or a missing input with its consequence (e.g. no airway pressure). A missing input is warned once, where it is read. A recording with all it needs and no problem has no warning; the logs of segmentation and indices follow the same rules.
  • Technical logs go through Python logging (logger names fasteit.preprocessing.*). The library never configures logging: the script or application decides where the messages go, e.g. logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) in a notebook, or stdout collected by Docker in an application.

docs.title: 6. Limits
docs.text:
• Checked against eitprocessing (946 breaths, two patients and a volunteer) and the pressures on four PEEP trials (notebook 06), not against a gold standard. Dräger PulmoVista and adults only (respiratory rate 6-60/min).
  • Breaths are timed on the impedance, not on the ventilator: asynchrony is not detected, and breaths within about 15 s of a sudden change of EELI are unreliable.
  • PEEP is read at the airway opening, without intrinsic PEEP (with intrinsic PEEP the driving pressure is overestimated); the driving pressure is that of the respiratory system, in a passive patient.
  • The plateau needs a hold of at least 0.5 s (or a flat pressure in pressure control) and is not validated against the ventilator. Holds, pressure control, Medibus and Timpel pressures and the tidal volume from the curves are tested on synthetic data only.
  • The tidal volume is the one the ventilator measures, leaks and circuit compression included.

plot_segmentation(load_data("P01_T0.bin"), segments, title="P01, T0")

The global impedance of the file (global_impedance: the sum of the pixels, with a gap where a frame has missing pixels) with the segments as bands: phases coloured by protocol (blue tidal, orange PEEP trial), exclusions grey and hatched, PEEP steps placed by hand with their level. Below, the airway pressure in cmH2O when the file has it.

from fasteit.plotting import plot_breaths

plot_breaths(trial)        # also a recording, TidalFeatures or PeepTrialFeatures

Here trial is the result of segment_peep_trial (analyse a recording).

Each breath is a marker at its end-inspiratory peak on the signal the breaths were found on:

Marker Breath filled blue circle used for the indices: the valid breaths of the phase (tidal), the breaths analysed in each step (PEEP trial) empty blue circle valid but not used: outside the phase, or in the first seconds of a step, or beyond the last 10 orange triangle flagged by a quality check grey cross excluded (the excluded parts are grey hatched bands)
