docs.title: fastEIT - Segmentation Layer (PEEP trials)
docs.text:
The segmentation layer (layer 2b) takes a preprocessed recording (EITRecording) and splits it by protocol. For a PEEP trial it finds the PEEP steps from the PEEP of each breath, chooses the breaths analysed in each step and gives each step its driving pressure and tidal volume. It is still preparation of the data: the clinical indices (EELI, TIV, compliance, Costa) come in layer 3 (features.md).

The PEEP, plateau and tidal volume of each breath are read in layer 2 (preprocessing.md, section 3), in cmH2O and mL for every vendor. The evidence for the pressure readings and the step detection is in notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb (four decremental PEEP trials from two patients). The 15 s left out after each change, the 10 (at least 5) breaths analysed and the 0.5 cmH2O tolerance are protocol choices.

  1. Entry point
  2. Steps
  3. Driving pressure and tidal volume of each step
  4. Recordings with more than one protocol
  5. Output
  6. Limits

docs.title: 1. Entry point
docs.text:
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext, Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

context = RecordingContext(protocol="peep_trial", tidal_volume_ml=450)  # Vt optional
recording = preprocess(load_data("peep_trial.bin"), context=context)
trial = segment_peep_trial(recording)

trial.steps              # one row per PEEP step: level, breaths, driving pressure, Vt
trial.analysed_breaths   # the breaths to analyse, with PEEP, plateau, driving pressure
print("\n".join(trial.log))

Without a pressure signal (or to choose the breaths yourself) the steps are placed by hand: for each step, a segment around the breaths to analyse (e.g. the 10 stable breaths chosen on the figure), with the PEEP level of the step (cmH2O):

steps = [
    Segment(60, 100, category="peep_step", parameters={"peep": 16}),
    Segment(110, 150, category="peep_step", parameters={"peep": 14}),
]
trial = segment_peep_trial(recording, peep_steps=steps)

Steps placed by hand replace the automatic ones, and a segment is the selection of breaths to analyse: every valid breath entirely inside it is analysed, with no time left out after the change of PEEP and no limit of 10 (those rules apply only to the steps found from the pressure). A breath cut by the edge of the segment, or with a quality flag, is left out: draw the segment a little wider than the breaths chosen. An inspiratory hold is looked for only inside the segment: include its breath, or type the plateau or the driving pressure. Without a pressure signal the plateau read on the ventilator can be typed with the step, parameters={"peep": 16, "plateau": 28}, or directly the driving pressure, parameters={"peep": 16, "driving_pressure": 12} (e.g. in pressure control, where it is set), and so can the tidal volume, parameters={"peep": 16, "tidal_volume": 450}. When there is a pressure signal, a typed PEEP more than 1 cmH2O from the measured one gives a warning. Parameters are in SegmentationConfig.

docs.title: 2. Steps
docs.text:
# Step Module 1 Breaths of the PEEP trial phase, with the PEEP and plateau of each breath read in layer 2 pipeline 2 Steps: a new step when 3 breaths in a row are more than 1 cmH2O (half of the step of the protocol) from the current level and within 1 cmH2O of each other; level = median PEEP. Excluded breaths (maneuvers) do not count peep_steps 3 Breaths analysed: the first 15 s after each change are left out; then the last valid breaths whose PEEP is within 0.5 cmH2O of the step level (a breath without a PEEP reading is not analysed), up to 10; fewer than 5 give a warning peep_steps 4 Step table: level of the protocol, driving pressure and tidal volume of each step pipeline

Level of the protocol (peep_set). The PEEP trial follows the protocol, the same for every patient, while the measured level is noisy and in cmH2O (10 mbar set on a Dräger ventilator is 10.2 cmH2O). Each step gets the nearest PEEP level of the protocol, given as SegmentationConfig(peep_levels=(16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0)), after removing the offset common to all steps (in a trial of notebook 06 every step read 0.6 cmH2O above the set level, and 1.1 cmH2O at PEEP 0, nearer to 2 than to 0). A step more than step_threshold (half of the step of the protocol) from every level gets none, with a warning; without the levels of the protocol peep_set is empty. peep_set is the level to compare and average steps between patients; peep stays the measured one.

The event texts typed on the device are not used to cut the steps: in the trials of the notebook they were written from 2 s after to 14 s before the change of pressure.

docs.title: 3. Driving pressure and tidal volume of each step
docs.text:
The driving pressure of each step (the input of compliance in layer 3) works with the usual protocols:

Protocol Driving pressure of the step (driving_pressure_source) Volume control with a continuous end-inspiratory pause median of the analysed breaths ("breaths") Volume control with one inspiratory hold per step median of the breaths with a hold, one is enough ("hold") Pressure control the flat inspiratory pressure is read as plateau ("breaths"), valid if the flow is zero at the end of inspiration No pressure signal typed with the step placed by hand ("typed")

The tidal volume of each step turns compliance into mL/cmH2O and EELI changes into mL. In order (tidal_volume_source):

Source How tidal_volume_source Typed for each step in the segment of a step placed by hand, or segment_peep_trial(recording, tidal_volumes=[450, 460, None, ...]), one per step in time order (e.g. the mean of each step on the case report form) "typed" Typed for the recording RecordingContext(tidal_volume_ml=450): the volume set in volume control, only when it is the same in every step (in pressure control it changes with PEEP: type it per step) "typed_recording" Measured median of the analysed breaths, from the volume or flow curve of the ventilator (layer 2) "breaths"

Without any of them the tidal volume is missing and compliance stays in EIT units. A typed volume outside 100-1500 mL, or more than 15 % from the one measured on the analysed breaths of the step, gives a warning: a typing error, or one volume typed for a trial in pressure control. How the tidal volume is used in layer 3, and the assumptions of each use (compliance of the respiratory system, volume of a region, change of EELI in mL), are in features.md.

docs.title: 4. Recordings with more than one protocol
docs.text:
A recording can contain, for example, a tidal baseline and then a PEEP trial. Each part is a phase with its own protocol, and the segmentation is limited to the PEEP trial phase:

phase = Segment(150, 600, category="phase", label="peep_trial")
trial = segment_peep_trial(recording, phase=phase)

Breaths outside the phase (or cut by its edges) have peep_step = -1 and are never analysed. A part with no planned analysis (for example an airway opening pressure maneuver) is simply an exclusion of preprocess(): its breaths are never analysed and do not count when the steps are found. Without a phase the whole recording is segmented.

docs.title: 5. Output
docs.text:
PeepTrial fields:

Field Content recording, config the preprocessed recording and the parameters used source "pressure" or "manual" phase the PEEP trial part of the recording, or None for the whole recording steps step, peep (level), peep_set (level of the protocol), start_time, end_time, n_breaths, n_analysed, enough, plateau, driving_pressure, driving_pressure_source, n_driving_pressure, enough_driving_pressure, tidal_volume, tidal_volume_source breaths the breath table of the recording (with peep, plateau, driving_pressure, tidal_volume) plus peep_step, analysed log what the segmentation did: checks passed (OK:), facts, warnings (WARNING:)

Pressures are in cmH2O and volumes in mL for every vendor (preprocess() converts the Dräger mbar, 1 mbar = 1.02 cmH2O). The channels they come from are recording.pressure_channel and recording.tidal_volume_channel.

docs.title: 6. Limits
docs.text:
• Tested on four decremental trials from two patients (volume control with an end-inspiratory pause, Dräger PressurePod); other ventilation modes and pressure sources on synthetic data only.

Research use only - not a medical device.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
Configuration dataclasses for the fasteit pipeline.

Single source of truth for tuneable parameters. Parsers and algorithms read values from here - change once, propagates everywhere.

Structure

PreprocessingConfig - layer 2: cardiac filter, breaths, lung mask, regions, pressures and tidal volume of each breath SegmentationConfig - layer 2b: PEEP steps of a PEEP trial and the breaths analysed AnalysisConfig - layer 3: clinical indices (recruitment-to-inflation ratio) Config - top-level container for pipeline sections

Rates and frequencies are given per minute here, as read on a monitor; the preprocessing functions work in Hz and the pipeline converts.

Usage

from fasteit.config import Config

cfg = Config()

docs.title: PreprocessingConfig dataclass
docs.text:
PreprocessingConfig(heart_rate_bpm: float | None = None, moving_average_seconds: float = 0.1, breath_short_seconds: float = 0.5, breath_long_seconds: float = 20.0, ti_ratio_low: float = 0.2, ti_ratio_high: float = 0.6, local_window_breaths: int = 21, amplitude_ratio_low: float = 0.5, amplitude_ratio_high: float = 2.0, duration_ratio_high: float = 2.0, lung_mask_threshold_fraction: float = 0.15, exclusion_margin_seconds: float = 0.5)

Parameters of the preprocessing layer (layer 2).

Frozen: a recording keeps the exact parameters it was made with. To change one, make a new config, e.g. dataclasses.replace(config, heart_rate_bpm=80).

Only the choices a study may change are here; the details of the methods taken from eitprocessing or fixed by the evidence are constants of their modules (cardiac_filter, breaths, breath_quality, lung_mask, breath_pressures, tidal_volume). Evidence: notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb (section in brackets).

Attributes:

Name Type Description heart_rate_bpm float | None

Heart rate entered by the user (beats/min), e.g. from the monitor. If given, the MDN filter removes the cardiac component; if None, only the moving average is applied. The heart rate is never estimated from the data: the estimate was wrong in 2 of 11 recordings and a wrong heart rate close to the respiratory rate damages the breaths (section 5b). It is a snapshot: a heart rate that drifts during the recording, or an arrhythmia such as atrial fibrillation, is not removed by the MDN filter.

moving_average_seconds float

Width of the centred moving average used when no heart rate is given (section 5c): the smooth() of the original MATLAB analysis scripts, in seconds so that it behaves the same at 20 and 50 Hz. It leaves the cardiac component almost untouched (a 100/min oscillation keeps about 96 % of its amplitude at 50 Hz, 91 % at 20 Hz).

breath_short_seconds, breath_long_seconds

A breath shorter or longer than this is flagged (flag_short, flag_long; roadmap task 4.11). 0.5 s is 120 breaths/min, below the 2/3 s minimum of the detection, so it mainly catches detection artefacts; above 20 s: a pause, an apnoea or a missed breath (section 8).

ti_ratio_low, ti_ratio_high

A breath with Ti/Ttot outside this range is flagged (flag_suspect_ti_ratio). Ti/Ttot here is the rise fraction of the impedance curve, a plausibility check on the detection, not a clinical judgement (roadmap task 4.11, section 8).

local_window_breaths int

Breaths, centred on each breath, whose median is the reference for the outlier flags: 21 are about 40 s at 30 breaths/min, long enough to ignore one event, short enough to follow a PEEP change (section 8).

amplitude_ratio_low, amplitude_ratio_high

A breath with an amplitude below or above these times the local median is flagged (flag_amplitude_outlier; section 8).

duration_ratio_high float

A breath longer than this times the local median duration is flagged (flag_duration_outlier), e.g. two breaths merged into one.

lung_mask_threshold_fraction float

A pixel is lung when its mean TIV (and, for the watershed, its amplitude) is at least this fraction of the maximum TIV (eitprocessing WatershedLungspace default; sections 7, 7b).

exclusion_margin_seconds float

Every exclusion (manual or from the device) is widened by this margin on both sides, because the forward-backward filters spread an artifact over the neighbouring samples (the margin around invalid data of eitprocessing BreathDetection).

docs.title: SegmentationConfig dataclass
docs.text:
SegmentationConfig(step_threshold: float = 1.0, analysis_skip_seconds: float = 15.0, analysis_max_breaths: int = 10, analysis_min_breaths: int = 5, peep_levels: tuple[float, ...] | None = None)

Parameters of the PEEP trial segmentation (layer 2b).

Protocol choices tested on four decremental trials (notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb, section in brackets); pressures in cmH2O. The details of the step finding are constants of peep_steps.

Attributes:

Name Type Description step_threshold float

Half of the PEEP step of the protocol (1 for steps of 2): a new step starts when 3 breaths in a row are further than this from the current level and within this of each other; a breath is analysed only if its PEEP is within half of this of the level of its step (section 3, 5).

analysis_skip_seconds float

In each step the breaths in this time after the change of PEEP are not analysed, as EELI is still moving (section 5).

analysis_max_breaths, analysis_min_breaths

Then the last valid breaths of the step are analysed, up to analysis_max_breaths; fewer than analysis_min_breaths give a warning (section 5).

peep_levels tuple[float, ...] | None

PEEP levels of the protocol, e.g. (16, 14, ..., 0). Each step gets the nearest one as peep_set, after removing the offset common to all steps, so that steps can be compared between patients (the measured PEEP is noisy, and 10 mbar set on a Dräger ventilator is 10.2 cmH2O); none, with a warning, if further than step_threshold. None: peep_set is empty.

docs.title: tables
docs.text:
The results as tables (layer 4): one analysis, a whole study, CSV files.

One analysis is the output of layer 3 for one phase of a recording (TidalFeatures or PeepTrialFeatures). Its tables start every row with the keys patient_id, label (the recording, e.g. a time point) and phase (the part analysed):

  • recordings: one row per analysis: file, breaths, results of a PEEP trial;
  • breaths: one row per breath of the phase;
  • steps: one row per PEEP step (PEEP trials only);
  • settings: the parameters, the context and the version of fastEIT used;
  • log: the messages of every layer, with their level (ok, info, warning).

The objects of layers 2-3 store each value once; here they are joined, so that a breath or a step is one row with everything (times, quality, pressures, volumes, indices). Regional values are columns named {index}__{region}, for the halves of the lung (ventral, dorsal, right, left; the layers and the quadrants stay in the objects), with two underscores because both names can contain one: in R tidyr::pivot_longer(contains("__"), names_to = c("index", "region"), names_sep = "__") gives back one row per region.

docs.title: pipeline
docs.text:
Clinical indices of a tidal recording or of a PEEP trial (layer 3).

Definitions and evidence: notebooks/07_clinical_indices.ipynb (section 5):

  • EELI and TIV of a breath: one sample at the frames of the layer 2 breaths, on the signal inside the lung mask; EELI at the start of the breath, TIV = peak - start (TREND: Frerichs et al., Thorax 2017, DOI: 10.1136/thoraxjnl-2016-208357);
  • per breath: TIV, EELI and share by region, GI, centre of ventilation, respiratory rate, compliance in EIT units (TIV / driving pressure) and in mL/cmH2O (tidal volume / driving pressure); with a tidal volume, the TIV and compliance of each region in mL (share x tidal volume);
  • tidal recording: median and quartiles over the valid breaths;
  • PEEP trial: per step, medians of the analysed breaths, compliance (also as % of the best step), Costa collapse and overdistension, changes vs the previous and the first step (EELI in tidal volumes and in mL, compliance); for the trial, the crossing PEEP, the best PEEP and the recruitment-to-inflation ratio, global and by region.

The tables hold the keys (breath_id, step, peep, region) and what this layer computes; what layers 2 and 2b measured stays in recording.breaths, trial.breaths and trial.steps, reached from the same object.

docs.title: costa
docs.text:
Collapse and overdistension in a PEEP trial, from the compliance of each pixel.

Costa et al., Intensive Care Med 2009;35:1132-1137, DOI: 10.1007/s00134-009-1447-y; formulas as reported by Shono and Kotani, J Intensive Care 2019;7:4, DOI: 10.1186/s40560-019-0358-4 (notebooks/07_clinical_indices.ipynb, section 4):

  • compliance of a pixel at a step = TIV of the pixel / driving pressure of the step;
  • each pixel has its best compliance, at its best PEEP;
  • at a step with a PEEP below the best PEEP of the pixel, its loss of compliance as % of its best is collapse; above, overdistension;
  • collapse (overdistension) of a step = mean of the pixel %, weighted by the best compliance of each pixel, over the pixels of the lung mask;
  • the crossing of the two curves is the PEEP with the best balance between them.

Compliance stays in EIT units: the method needs no tidal volume. An error common to all the pixels of a step (its driving pressure, the share of the tidal volume seen by the slice) shifts them together and appears as collapse or overdistension.

The loss of a pixel is at most 100 %.

docs.title: recruitment
docs.text:
Recruitment-to-inflation ratio (R/I) of a PEEP trial, from EIT.

R/I (Chen et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2020;201:178-187, DOI: 10.1164/rccm.201902-0334OC): when PEEP falls from a high to a low level, the lung loses more volume than its compliance at the low PEEP predicts; the excess is the volume that was recruited at the high PEEP:

predicted volume  = C_low x dPEEP
recruited volume  = dEELV - C_low x dPEEP
R/I               = (recruited volume / dPEEP) / C_low

With EIT the change of end-expiratory lung volume is the change of EELI converted with the tidal volume / TIV of the low PEEP step (Wang et al., Med Sci Monit 2020;26:e922609, DOI: 10.12659/MSM.922609), and C_low = tidal volume / driving pressure of the low step. The tidal volume cancels in R/I, which therefore needs only EIT and the driving pressure:

R/I = dEELI / (C_EIT,low x dPEEP) - 1,   with C_EIT,low = TIV_low / driving_low

and it applies to a region with its own EELI and EIT compliance. The original method reads one expiration after the drop of PEEP; here each level is the equilibrium EELI of a step, as in Wang 2020.

roi_signals: ndarray

4 ventro-dorsal strip signals (equal horizontal strips). Shape (N, 4).

Each strip sums 8 rows of the 32×32 image: strip 0 = rows 0- 7 (ventral) strip 1 = rows 8-15 (mid-ventral) strip 2 = rows 16-23 (mid-dorsal) strip 3 = rows 24-31 (dorsal)

These are the four horizontal layers of the PulmoVista display (its ROI 1-4 are strips 0-3 here), on the whole image. docs.text:
Clinical indices of a recording (layer 3), as tables ready for a database or R.

  • TidalFeatures - indices of each breath of a recording, and their summary
  • PeepTrialFeatures - indices of each breath and of each PEEP step of a PEEP trial

Each object holds everything: its tables, and the objects of the layers before it (features.trial.recording.breaths...). Each value is stored once: the tables of layer 3 have the keys (breath_id, step, peep, region) and what layer 3 computes; what layers 2 and 2b measured (times, quality, pressures, steps) stays in their own tables, joined on the keys. The tables are "long" by region (one row per breath, or step, and region), so that they can be joined with the clinical data (patient, position, side) at the time of the analysis.

Format summary (reverse-engineered from PulmoVista 500 output, cross-referenced with EIDORS read_draeger_header/read_draeger_file):

Byte 0..11            : preamble - 3 × int32 LE
                        [0:4]  format_version (always 51)
                        [4:8]  sep_offset      (variable, file-specific)
                        [8:12] unknown_int
Byte 12..sep_offset-1 : ASCII header (latin-1, "key: value\r\n" lines)
Byte sep_offset..+7   : separator b'**\r\n\r\n\r\n' (8 bytes)
Byte sep_offset+8..   : binary frames, each 5495 bytes

docs.text:
Bases: BaseParser

Parser for Dräger PulmoVista 500 .asc tabular exports.

The .asc file contains several sections: - ASCII header - recording metadata (file, length, filter settings) - Dynamic Image - 32×32 pixel table, one row per frame (skipped) - Tidal Image - 32×32 pixel table, breath-averaged (skipped) - Tidal Variations - breath-averaged summary (~11 columns, skipped) - Continuous waveforms - frame-by-frame signal table (~68 columns, parsed)

This parser targets the continuous waveforms section, identified by its header row starting with Image and containing more than 20 tab-separated columns. The other sections have ≤11 columns and are deliberately skipped.

Header metadata is preserved in ContinuousSignalData.metadata.

Format source: reverse-engineered from PulmoVista 500 exports. See docs/reverse_eng/draeger_bin_format.ipynb for field-level findings.

docs.title: timpel_parser
docs.text:
Timpel tabular EIT file parser.

Parses Timpel comma-separated export files (.csv / .txt) into ReconstructedFrameData.

File format (1030 columns per row, no header, comma-delimited): cols 0-1023 32×32 reconstructed pixel impedance (row-major, arbitrary units) col 1024 airway pressure (cmH₂O) col 1025 flow (L/s) col 1026 volume (L) col 1027 min_flag 1 = expiration trough detected, 0 = none col 1028 max_flag 1 = inspiration peak detected, 0 = none col 1029 qrs_flag 1 = QRS complex detected, 0 = none

Sentinel: −1000.0 → NaN (electrode disconnection or N/A channel). Sampling frequency: 50 Hz (fixed by device firmware; no timestamps in file).

Format reference: eitprocessing timpel.py loader (Apache-2.0) https://github.com/EIT-ALIVE/eitprocessing Somhorst P et al., "eitprocessing", JOSS 2026;11(117):8179 DOI: 10.21105/joss.08179

Figures to review a recording before trusting its numbers.

  • plot_segmentation(raw, segments): the parts chosen by the user (phases, exclusions, PEEP steps placed by hand) on the global signal and the airway pressure of the file, before preprocess();

docs.title: pipeline
docs.text:
preprocess(): from the parsed frames to a recording ready for analysis (layer 2).

Fixed order of the steps (notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb): 1. time in seconds, pixel copy with the device "no data" values as NaN; 2. frames with missing pixel data filled and excluded; 3. respiratory rate from the spectrum, cardiac step (MDN with a heart rate given by the user, otherwise only a moving average); 4. breath detection on the global signal (sum of all pixels); 5. quality flags and exclusions of each breath; 6. lung mask from the valid breaths, regions of interest, regional signals; 7. auxiliary signals (pressures, flow, volume, device markers) with "no data" as NaN, in the same units for every vendor (cmH2O, L/s, mL); 8. airway pressures of each breath: PEEP, plateau, driving pressure (notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb); 9. inspiratory tidal volume of each breath, from the ventilator curves.

Every step writes what it did in EITRecording.log (saved with the results) and in the Python logger fasteit.preprocessing.pipeline (technical log, configured by the application, not here).

docs.title: cardiac_filter
docs.text:
Cardiac filtering of the pixel signals.

Policy (notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb, section 5c): - heart rate given by the user -> MDN filter; - no heart rate -> only a light moving average, the cardiac component is NOT removed.

All functions work along axis 0 (time). Rates are in Hz here; the configuration uses breaths or beats per minute, and the caller converts with SECONDS_PER_MINUTE. Parameters have no defaults here on purpose: they live only in fasteit.config.PreprocessingConfig.

Valid for adult recordings only (respiratory rate 6-60/min); not for neonates, paediatric patients or high-frequency oscillation.

docs.text:
respiratory_rate(global_signal: ndarray, fs: float, min_bpm: float, max_bpm: float, window_seconds: float) -> float

Respiratory rate (Hz) from the power spectrum of the global signal.

Same method as the respiratory part of eitprocessing RateDetection (v1.8.8; Somhorst et al., JOSS 2026;11(117):8179, DOI: 10.21105/joss.08179): Welch spectrum (Hann window, 50 % overlap, mean removed), highest peak between min_bpm and max_bpm, refined with a parabola through the peak and its two neighbours.

It is the mean rate of the whole signal, not of single breaths. In the evidence notebook (section 4) the largest difference from the device breath markers was 1.7 breaths/min over 11 recordings (rates 10-42/min). With a 30 s window the spectral bins are 2/min apart before the refinement.

docs.title: mdn_filter
docs.text:
mdn_filter(signals: ndarray, fs: float, respiratory_rate_hz: float, heart_rate_hz: float, notch_half_width_hz: float, upper_limit_hz: float, order: int) -> np.ndarray

Remove the cardiac component with a multiple digital notch (MDN) filter.

Wisse et al., "Improved filtering methods to suppress cardiovascular contamination in EIT recordings", Physiol Meas 2024, DOI: 10.1088/1361-6579/ad46e3. Implementation follows eitprocessing MDNFilter (v1.8.8):

  1. one band-stop (Butterworth, zero phase) around each cardiac harmonic k * heart_rate ± notch_half_width, up to upper_limit_hz;
  2. the first band-stop never starts below (respiratory_rate + heart_rate) / 2, so that it does not cut the breathing;
  3. a low-pass at upper_limit_hz removes what is left above it.

Zero-phase filtering (forward and backward) doubles the effective order of each filter. Apply it to the whole recording, not to short pieces: narrow band-stops of this order have transients of several seconds at both ends.

The heart rate comes from the user (section 5c of the evidence notebook). It is a snapshot: a heart rate drifting more than about ±10/min during the recording, or an arrhythmia such as atrial fibrillation, is not removed by fixed notches. A heart rate above upper_limit_hz + notch_half_width_hz (about 230/min) gets no notch, only the low-pass.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default signals ndarray

Array with time on axis 0 (pixels or a 1-D signal).

required fs float

Sampling frequency in Hz.

required respiratory_rate_hz float

Respiratory rate in Hz.

required heart_rate_hz float

Heart rate in Hz.

required notch_half_width_hz float

Half width of each band-stop, in Hz.

required upper_limit_hz float

Highest frequency filtered, in Hz.

required order int

Butterworth order of each band-stop and of the low-pass.

required

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

Filtered array of the same shape as signals.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

if a rate is not positive, the heart rate is not above the respiratory rate, fs is too low for upper_limit_hz, the signal is too short for the filter, or it has NaN at some frames only.

docs.title: exclusions
docs.text:
Parts of a recording excluded from the analysis.

Exclusions come from the user (source="manual") or from the device (source="device": frames with a timing error or with missing pixel data). They are widened by a margin, because the forward-backward filters spread an artifact over the neighbouring samples, and a breath that touches an exclusion is marked excluded: it stays in the breath table (fastEIT design decision D5).

Frames with missing pixel data are also filled with the nearest valid frame, so that the filters can run on a continuous signal; the filled frames are excluded.

docs.title: breaths
docs.text:
Breath detection on the global impedance signal.

Reimplementation of eitprocessing BreathDetection (v1.8.8; Somhorst et al., JOSS 2026;11(117):8179, DOI: 10.21105/joss.08179). It gives the same breaths as eitprocessing on 11 regular real recordings (notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb, section 8) and on synthetic signals with a spike and with small breaths. This shows equivalence with eitprocessing, not accuracy against a gold standard.

One change: breaths close to invalid data are flagged, not removed.

A breath is a triplet of frame indices: start (valley), peak, end (next valley). Impedance is assumed to rise with inspiration (as in the Draeger .bin pixels).

Limitations (to keep in mind when reading Ti, Te and the respiratory rate): - the valley is the minimum of impedance, i.e. of lung volume, not the start of the inspiratory effort or the ventilator trigger; the peak includes any inspiratory pause. Timings are impedance-based and not interchangeable with the ventilator values; - patient-ventilator asynchrony is not detected: an ineffective effort is usually not a peak, and two inspirations without a valley between them become one breath; - the 15 s baseline follows slow EELI drift, but after a sudden EELI step (PEEP change, recruitment) the breaths within about 15 s of the step are unreliable.

docs.title: lung_mask
docs.text:
Functional lung mask with the watershed method.

Reimplementation of eitprocessing WatershedLungspace (v1.8.8; Somhorst et al., JOSS 2026;11(117):8179, DOI: 10.21105/joss.08179), with the pixel amplitude in its "phase shift" mode (PixelBreath) and the small-region filter FilterROIBySize. Checked to give the same masks as eitprocessing on 11 real recordings when every breath is used (notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb, sections 7b and 9).

The mask is the VENTILATED lung, not the anatomical lung: a collapsed region with a TIV below the threshold is outside it.

Steps: 1. TIV map: pixel value at the end of inspiration of the global signal minus the value at its start, mean over the breaths; 2. amplitude map: the same, but on each pixel's own timing, found by cross-correlation with the global signal (it catches pixels that inflate late, e.g. pendelluft); 3. threshold: a fraction of the maximum of the TIV map, applied to both maps; 4. watershed: the amplitude map is split into regions around its local maxima; a region is kept if its maximum is inside the TIV mask. Mask = kept regions inside the amplitude mask; 5. islands smaller than a minimum size are removed.

The watershed assumes smooth images, with high amplitude in the centre of the lung and low amplitude at its edges, as reconstructed EIT images are.

docs.title: regions
docs.text:
Regions of interest inside the lung mask.

Orientation of Draeger images (PulmoVista 500 instructions for use): seen from the feet, like a CT slice. Row 0 is ventral; column 0 is the patient's RIGHT, column 31 the patient's left. Consistent with the power at the heart rate per pixel (notebooks/05_preprocessing_choices.ipynb, section 9). Verified on Draeger only.

Regions (section 9): - ventral/dorsal halves and four layers are cut on the vertical extent of the lung (first to last row of the mask), not on the image, so "dorsal" is always the dorsal part of that lung wherever the lungs sit in the image. Same approach as the createSummersROIs.m script of the original MATLAB analysis; the published source of this approach is still to be found; - right/left halves are split at the image midline (between columns 15 and 16), the sternum-spine axis with the belt centred on the patient; - quadrants = ventral/dorsal x right/left; - every region is intersected with the lung mask.

Limit: these regions are relative to the VENTILATED lung. If the dorsal lung collapses, its pixels leave the mask and "dorsal" becomes the dorsal half of what is still ventilated, so the ventral/dorsal split hides part of a ventral shift of ventilation. Indices meant to show a shift of ventilation (centre of ventilation, dorsal fraction, silent spaces) must be computed in image coordinates, not on these regions.

Not the same as ReconstructedFrameData.roi_signals (layer 1), which are four fixed strips of 8 image rows each.

docs.title: auxiliary
docs.text:
Auxiliary signals recorded with the images: pressures, flow, volume, device markers.

The parsers keep them as they are in the file (raw.aux_signals): for Draeger .bin the channels that were not available hold "no data" values (-1000, or a bit pattern read as about -3.4e38) instead of NaN, and each vendor has its own units. Here they are cleaned once, so the next layers read every vendor in the same way: "no data" as NaN and the same units, pressures in cmH2O, flow in L/s, volumes in mL.

The signals are not filtered and not filled: a missing value stays NaN.

docs.title: breath_pressures
docs.text:
Airway pressures of each breath: PEEP, plateau and driving pressure.

Read on the airway pressure curve (cmH2O), all from the same channel so that a constant offset of the sensor cancels in the driving pressure (notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb, sections 2 and 4). The PEEP of a breath is the end-expiratory pressure at the airway opening: the PEEP applied by the ventilator, without intrinsic PEEP (that would need an end-expiratory occlusion), so it is a lower bound of the total PEEP; with intrinsic PEEP the driving pressure is overestimated and compliance underestimated. A breath whose pressure is missing (NaN) near its start gets NaN.

The EIT valley falls within about 0.1 s of it, but there the pressure already rises quickly (notebook 06, section 2).

docs.title: plateau_pressures
docs.text:
plateau_pressures(paw: ndarray, fs: float, onsets: ndarray, peeps: ndarray, window: tuple[float, float]) -> np.ndarray

Plateau pressure of each breath, read at the end of the end-inspiratory hold.

Between the start of inspiration of a breath and the next one: after the highest part of the breath (the peak in volume control, the flat pressure in pressure control), the start of expiration is the steepest fall of the pressure in the 0.3 s before it comes back within 2 of the next PEEP; the plateau is the median pressure from window[0] to window[1] seconds before it (notebook 06, section 4).

A valid plateau needs at least 0.5 s between the highest part and the expiration: an end-inspiratory hold with zero flow in volume control (continuous pause, or an inspiratory hold done by hand), or the flat inspiratory pressure in pressure control, which is a plateau only if the flow is zero at the end of inspiration. Otherwise the plateau is NaN: the reading would fall on the relaxation after the peak, and the peak pressure is never used instead because it includes the resistive pressure.

docs.title: tidal_volume
docs.text:
Tidal volume of each breath from the ventilator curves (mL).

The inspiratory tidal volume: in volume control it is the volume delivered, the one set on the ventilator. It is read on the volume curve, or on the flow curve by integrating the inspiratory flow, in a window around the inspiration of each EIT breath. It is the volume measured by the ventilator: with a leak (non-invasive ventilation, a leaking cuff) it includes the leak, and without compensation of the compressible volume of the circuit it includes that too.

Tested on synthetic curves only: the recordings available have no volume or flow curve. Inspiratory flow is taken as positive, as recorded by the ventilators.

docs.text:
segment_peep_trial(): split a preprocessed PEEP trial into PEEP steps (layer 2b).

Steps (notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb, section 7): 1. breaths of the PEEP trial phase, with the PEEP and plateau read in layer 2 (EITRecording.breaths); 2. PEEP steps: placed by hand if given, otherwise found from the PEEP of each breath; 3. breaths analysed in each step, and the step table.

Split a preprocessed PEEP trial into PEEP steps and choose the breaths analysed.

A recording can contain more than one protocol, e.g. a tidal baseline and then a PEEP trial: phase limits the segmentation to the PEEP trial. A part that is not analysed at all (e.g. a maneuver) is an exclusion of preprocess() instead: its breaths are never analysed and do not count when the steps are found.

Output of preprocess().

If given, they replace the steps found from the pressure, and the breaths analysed are the valid breaths inside them.

The PEEP trial part of the recording: a segment with category="phase" and label="peep_trial". If None, the whole recording.

docs.title: peep_steps
docs.text:
PEEP steps of a PEEP trial and the breaths analysed in each step.

Steps come from the PEEP of each breath (EITRecording.breaths) or are placed by hand as segments with their PEEP level; steps placed by hand win over the automatic ones (notebooks/06_peep_trial_segmentation.ipynb, sections 3, 5 and 7).

docs.title: find_steps
docs.text:
find_steps(peep: ndarray, threshold: float, min_breaths: int, agreement: float) -> np.ndarray

First breath of each PEEP step.

A new step starts when min_breaths breaths in a row are further than threshold from the level of the current step and within agreement of each other; the level of the current step is the median PEEP of its breaths so far (of the first min_breaths breaths at the start). With min_breaths of 2 or more a single odd breath (a maneuver) cannot open a step. A breath without PEEP (NaN) takes the PEEP of the next breath that has one.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default peep ndarray

PEEP of each breath.

required threshold float

Half of the step of the protocol (e.g. 1 for steps of 2).

required min_breaths int

Breaths in a row needed to open a step.

required agreement float

Largest spread of those breaths.

required

Index of the first breath of each step; the first is always 0.

docs.title: protocol_levels
docs.text:
protocol_levels(levels: ndarray, protocol: Sequence[float] | None, tolerance: float) -> np.ndarray

PEEP level of the protocol of each step.

The measured PEEP of every step can be off the set level by about the same amount (mbar to cmH2O, PEEP valve: +0.6 cmH2O in every step of a trial of notebook 06, 1.1 cmH2O at PEEP 0, nearer to 2 than to 0). That offset, the median distance of the steps from their nearest level, is removed first; then each step gets the nearest level. A step further than tolerance from every level (a level that is not in the protocol) gets NaN. An offset of half a step or more cannot be told apart from the next level.

docs.title: Analyse a recording
docs.text:
One recording, from the file to the tables, with the functions of each step called one after the other. Every value is in the objects and in the exported tables; nothing has to be computed by hand.

  1. A tidal recording
  2. A PEEP trial
  3. A recording with two parts
  4. Check the result
  5. Save the tables

docs.title: 1. A tidal recording
docs.text:
from fasteit.config import PreprocessingConfig
from fasteit.features import tidal_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess

raw = load_data("P01_T0.bin")
recording = preprocess(
    raw,
    config=PreprocessingConfig(heart_rate_bpm=85),   # optional: removes the cardiac component
    context=RecordingContext(patient_id="P01", label="T0", tidal_volume_ml=450),
)
tidal = tidal_features(recording)
What Where breaths found, with times, quality flags, PEEP, plateau, driving pressure, tidal volume recording.breaths EELI, TIV, GI, centre of ventilation, compliance of each breath tidal.breaths the same by region: ventral, dorsal, right, left (the objects also hold layers and quadrants; the exported tables have the four halves only) tidal.regions median and quartiles over the valid breaths tidal.summary what each step did: checks passed (OK:), facts, warnings (WARNING:) recording.log, tidal.log

Optional inputs. Without heart_rate_bpm the cardiac component is not removed (a 0.1 s moving average only). Without a tidal volume (typed, or measured on the ventilator curves) the values in mL stay empty and compliance is in EIT units only.

docs.title: 2. A PEEP trial
docs.text:
from fasteit.config import SegmentationConfig
from fasteit.features import peep_trial_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

recording = preprocess(
    load_data("P01_trial.bin"),
    context=RecordingContext(patient_id="P01", label="supine", protocol="peep_trial",
                             tidal_volume_ml=450),
)
trial = segment_peep_trial(
    recording,
    SegmentationConfig(peep_levels=(16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0)),   # the protocol
)
trial_features = peep_trial_features(trial)
What Where PEEP steps: measured level, level of the protocol (peep_set), breaths analysed, driving pressure, tidal volume trial.steps breaths with their step and whether they were analysed trial.breaths each step: compliance and % of the best, Costa collapse and overdistension, changes between steps trial_features.steps crossing PEEP, best PEEP, recruitment-to-inflation ratio (global and by region) trial_features.summary

The steps are found on the airway pressure. Without a pressure signal, or to choose the breaths yourself, place the steps by hand (cut a recording). With the levels of the protocol (peep_levels), each step also gets the level of the protocol (peep_set), and crossing PEEP and best PEEP are given on those levels when every step matches one; otherwise they are given on the measured PEEP, and the log says which. Without peep_levels, peep_set is empty and the measured PEEP is used.

docs.title: 3. A recording with two parts
docs.text:
A baseline at one PEEP and a PEEP trial in the same file: preprocess the whole file once (same filters, same lung mask), then analyse each part. Times are in seconds from the start of the file; cut a recording shows how to find them.

from fasteit.features import peep_trial_features, tidal_features
from fasteit.models import RecordingContext, Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

recording = preprocess(
    load_data("P02_T0.bin"),
    exclusions=[Segment(285, 300, label="movement")],
    context=RecordingContext(patient_id="P02", label="T0", tidal_volume_ml=450),
)
baseline = tidal_features(recording, phase=Segment(0, 290, "phase", "tidal"))
trial = segment_peep_trial(recording, phase=Segment(300, 1500, "phase", "peep_trial"))
trial_features = peep_trial_features(trial)

Each part is an analysis of its own. A breath belongs to a part when it starts and ends inside it. In the exported tables the parts are told apart by the name of the phase (section 5). The exclusion is widened by 0.5 s on each side: see cut a recording.

docs.title: 4. Check the result
docs.text:
from fasteit.plotting import plot_breaths

plot_breaths(tidal)           # section 1: breaths used, flagged, excluded; lung mask
plot_breaths(trial)           # section 2: the same, with the steps and their level

Look at the figure before trusting the numbers: if a stretch of unstable breaths was analysed, exclude it and preprocess again (review figures). Then read the logs (recording.log, trial.log, features.log): a recording with all it needs and no problem has only checks (OK:) and facts; each WARNING: says what is missing or wrong and what it changes.

docs.title: 5. Save the tables
docs.text:
from fasteit.export import combine_tables, recording_tables, write_csv

write_csv(recording_tables(tidal), "results/P01_T0/")          # one analysis (section 1)

tables = combine_tables([                                       # two parts (section 3)
    recording_tables(baseline, phase="baseline"),
    recording_tables(trial_features, phase="trial"),
])
write_csv(tables, "results/study/")

Every row starts with patient_id, label and phase, so the tables of many recordings can be put together and joined with the clinical data (export). Only Dräger .bin and Timpel files can be analysed; .eit and .asc are read but not analysed (supported files).

How each step works: preprocessing, segmentation, clinical indices.

docs.title: Cut a recording
docs.text:
Parts of a recording are described by time intervals (Segment), in seconds from the start of the file. There are three kinds:

Kind What it does Example exclusion its breaths are never analysed (movement, suction, recalibration) Segment(600, 640, label="movement") phase a part with its own protocol, analysed on its own Segment(0, 290, "phase", "tidal") PEEP step placed by hand the breaths of a step and its PEEP level, when there is no pressure signal or to choose the breaths Segment(60, 100, category="peep_step", parameters={"peep": 16})

docs.title: 1. Find the times
docs.text:
Look at the whole recording before cutting it: the global signal and the airway pressure, with the segments drawn on top.

from fasteit.models import Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.plotting import plot_segmentation

raw = load_data("P02_T0.bin")
plot_segmentation(raw)                       # read the times on the x axis

segments = [
    Segment(0, 290, "phase", "tidal"),
    Segment(300, 1500, "phase", "peep_trial"),
    Segment(285, 300, label="movement"),
]
plot_segmentation(raw, segments)             # check the cuts before preprocessing

The times read on the figure are precise enough: what matters is which breaths fall inside, not the exact sample.

docs.title: 2. Use them
docs.text:
from fasteit.features import tidal_features
from fasteit.models import Segment
from fasteit.parsers.loader import load_data
from fasteit.preprocessing import preprocess
from fasteit.segmentation import segment_peep_trial

raw = load_data("P02_T0.bin")
segments = [
    Segment(0, 290, "phase", "tidal"),
    Segment(300, 1500, "phase", "peep_trial"),
    Segment(285, 300, label="movement"),
]
recording = preprocess(raw, exclusions=[s for s in segments if s.category == "exclusion"])
baseline = tidal_features(recording, phase=segments[0])
trial = segment_peep_trial(recording, phase=segments[1])

Steps placed by hand go to segment_peep_trial(recording, peep_steps=[...]), with the PEEP of each step and, if known, its plateau or driving pressure and tidal volume in parameters. The levels of the protocol (SegmentationConfig(peep_levels=...)) give each step its peep_set: see analyse a recording.

Only Dräger .bin and Timpel files (reconstructed images) can be cut and analysed.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A breath belongs to an interval when it starts and ends inside it: a breath cut by the edge of a phase or of a step is left out.
  • Exclusions are widened by 0.5 s on each side (filters spread an artifact over the next samples), and every breath that touches them is excluded. To exclude one breath only, use a short interval around its peak, not the whole breath.
  • Excluding is not cutting: the signal stays whole, with its original times, and the excluded breaths stay in the tables marked excluded.
  • A step placed by hand is the selection of breaths to analyse: all its valid breaths, for example the ten chosen on the figure.
  • One recording is one file. Two parts of the same file share the preprocessing (lung mask, filters); two files of the same patient are two recordings, each with its own.

Details: preprocessing (exclusions) and segmentation (phases and steps).
